=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
AssessmentIdentifier (E1144) is a unique number or alphanumeric code assigned to an assessment by a school, school system, a state, or other agency or entity.
Namespace (E3038) is the public web site address (URL), file or file transfer protocol (FTP) locator.
AssessmentTitle is required in the Ed-Fi model and is mandatory for the entity to be loaded into the individual operational data store (IODS). AssessmentTitle will not be promoted to the TSDS datamarts.
TitleOfAssessment (E1127) is the title or name of the assessment.
ReportAssessmentType (E1573) indicates the TEA Submissions (ECDS-PK and ECDS-KG) for which the assessment should be reported.
AcademicSubject (E1097) describes the content or subject area (e.g., arts, mathematics, reading, stenography, or a foreign language) of an assessment.
AssessedGradeLevel (E1129) indicates the typical grade level for which the assessment is designed.
## DR2
Assessment>AssessmentPerformanceLevel
The AssessmentPerformanceLevel common type defines the performance levels and the associated cut scores.
AssessmentReportingMethod (E1154) indicates the method that the administrator of the assessment uses to report the performance and achievement of all students. It may be a qualitative method such as performance level descriptors or a quantitative method such as a numerical grade or cut score. More than one type of reporting method may be used.
PerformanceLevel (E3077) is the performance level(s) defined for the assessment.
MaximumScore is required in the Ed-Fi model and is mandatory for the common type to be loaded into the Individual Operational Data Store (IODS). MaximumScore will not be promoted to the TSDS datamarts.
MinimumScore is required in the Ed-Fi model and is mandatory for the common type to be loaded into the Individual Operational Data Store (IODS). MinimumScore will not be promoted to the TSDS datamarts.

elements.definition_text: CalendarCode indicates a unique campus calendar of school days for a particular group of students on a campus. Students with the same CalendarCode have the same number of days taught in a particular reporting period at a campus.
elements.business_rules_text:
=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
Texas Education Code §25.081 requires that schools operate a school year for each campus that includes 75,600 minutes of school day operation over the course of the school year. TEC §48.005 contains provisions for certain groups of students to attend school based on Instructional Minutes; 32,400 for Prekindergarten and 43,200 for dropout or at-risk student programs. Open-enrollment charter schools approved prior to January 1, 2015, are permitted to operate on the basis of a 180-day calendar instead of 75,600 minutes.
The collection of the data in the School Calendar Domain is limited to the days students are planned to attend school and the days that are sub-planted with a waiver and the students do not actually attend school either for a partial day or a full day. Do not report school holidays, such as spring break, weekends, or any other time that staff and students are not expected to be at school. Do not include staff workdays that are not related to exercising the option of using a staff development waiver in lieu of a student instructional day.
Per TEC §25.081(g), a school cannot plan on Memorial Day being an operational day or student school day when building the calendar(s) for a campus and then ask for the waiver.
Active instructional campuses must report school calendar data.
Refer to the Student Attendance Accounting Handbook for additional details and rules related to operating a campus for 75,600 minutes per school year.
## GR2
PEIMS Fall Enrollment Submission (6):
The Calendar Entity is used in the PEIMS Fall Enrollment Submission in reference to the StudentSchoolAssociation Entity.
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
The Calendar Entity is reported for attendance purposes in the PEIMS Summer Submission.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
The Calendar Entity for the Optional Flexible School Day Program (OFSDP) Credit/Promotion Recovery Program, the Extended School Year Program, and the Additional Days School Year Program is reported in the PEIMS Extended Year Submission.
## GR3
Special Education Data System (SPEDS) - Summer Submission:
The Calendar Entity is used by the SPEDS - Summer Submission for students being evaluated for Special Education services (SPPI-11).
To calculate federal compliance data, TEA will utilize the Calendar Entity from the current year and may utilize the prior year PEIMS Summer accepted data.
CalendarType will be loaded in the landing zone but not promoted for the SPEDS - Summer Submission.

Special Requirements: ## SR1
Prekindergarten Programs (CalendarTypeDescriptors 04, 14, and 15):
Each prekindergarten program should have its own CalendarCode.
Half-day Prekindergarten programs report SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes and do not report SchoolDayOperationalMinutes.
JJAEP (CalendarTypeDescriptor 13):
Juvenile Justice Alternative Education Programs (JJAEPs) report days of operation based on 180 days/7 hours a day, and do not report SchoolDayOperationalMinutes OR SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes. Waivers for JJAEPs are issued by the Texas Juvenile Justice Department (TJJD) and not TEA. JJAEPs should only use CalendarWaiverEventTypeDescriptor 05 (JJAEP School Day Waiver Issued by TJJD).
DAEP (CalendarTypeDescriptor 06):
If a Disciplinary Alternative Education Program (DAEP) is housed on a regular campus, and their bell schedule matches the bell schedule of the regular campus, then it will not need a separate CalendarCode because it can safely be assumed that a track that met the 75,600 operational minute requirement would also meet the 43,200 instructional minute requirement.
If a DAEP is housed on a regular campus, and their bell schedule does not match the bell schedule of the regular campus, OR, if the DAEP has its own ID in AskTED, then it will need its own CalendarCode and use CalendarTypeDescriptor 06 (Disciplinary Alternative Education Program/Campus TEC 37.008).

=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
Each campus that reports at least one student in attendance during the course of the school year must also report school calendar data.
Because schools that operate a CalendarTypeDescriptor 01 (Standard Program 75,600 operation mins) are required to operate a school year consisting of at least 75,600 school day operational minutes, the sum of the data elements, SchoolDayOperationalMinutes and the SchoolDayWaiverMinutes should add up to at least 75,600 minutes.
## GR2
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
Texas Education Code 25.081 requires that schools operate a school year for each campus that includes 75,600 minutes of school day operation over the course of the school year. TEC 48.005 contains provisions for certain groups of students to attend school on the basis of Instructional Minutes; 32,400 for Prekindergarten and 43,200 for dropout or at-risk student programs. Open-enrollment charter schools approved prior to January 1, 2015 are permitted to operate on the basis of a 180-day calendar instead of 75,600 minutes.
The collection of the data on the CalendarDate Entity is limited to the days that students are planned to attend school and the days that are sub-planted with a waiver and the students do not actually attend school either for a partial day or a full day. Do not report school holidays, such as spring break, weekends, or any other time that staff and students are not expected to be at school. Do not include staff work days that are not related to exercising the option of using a staff development waiver in lieu of a student instruction day.
Because schools that operate a CalendarType 01 (Standard Program 75,600 operation mins) are required to operate a school year consisting of at least 75,600 school day operational minutes, the sum of the SchoolDayOperationalMinutes and the SchoolDayWaiverMinutes should add to at least 75,600 minutes.
Each campus that reports at least one student in attendance during the course of the school year must also report school calendar data.
Per TEC 25.081(g) a school cannot plan on Memorial Day being an operational day or student school day when building the calendar(s) for a campus and then ask for the waiver.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
The CalendarDate Entity for the Optional Flexible School Day Program (OFSDP) Credit/Promotion Recovery Program, the Extended School Year Program, and the Additional Days School Year (ADSY) Program is reported in the PEIMS Extended Year Submission.
## GR3
Special Education Data System (SPEDS) - Summer Submission:
The CalendarDate Entity is used by the SPEDS - Summer Submission for students being evaluated for Special Education services (SPPI-11).
For all students reported for SPPI-11, the current year CalendarDate Entity and prior year PEIMS Summer Accepted calendar data may be used for TEA to calculate the following:
- The number of instructional days needed to complete the student’s evaluation once the LEA receives consent.
- The number of instructional days left in the school year beginning the first instructional day after parental consent was received.
- The last instructional day of the school year.
Additionally, for students reporting a ConsentToEvaluationReceivedDate in one school year and an EligibilityDeterminationDate in a different school year, the SPEDS - Summer Submission will use the student’s 15th day of school from the CalendarDate Entity (current) to calculate the Federal compliance information.

Special Requirements: ## SR1
Prekindergarten Programs (CalendarType 04, 14, or, 15):
Each prekindergarten program should be on its own CalendarCode.
Half-day Prekindergarten programs report SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes and do not report SchoolDayOperationalMinutes.
JJAEP (CalendarType 13):
JJAEPs report days of operation based on 180 days/7 hours a day, and do not report SchoolDayOperationalMinutes OR SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes. Waivers for JJAEPs are issued by the Texas Juvenile Justice Department (TJJD) and not TEA. JJAEPs should only use CalendarWaiverEventTypeDescriptor 05 (JJAEP School Day Waiver Issued by Texas Juvenile Justice Department (TJJD)).
Additional Days School Year Program (CalendarType 16)
When reporting the calendar dates for the ADSY Program, use CalendarEventDescriptor 01 (Instructional Day). Waivers do not apply to this program.
Other CalendarTypes:
Dropout Recovery, DAEP, Correctional Facility, Residential Treatment Facility, Day Treatment Facility, Psychiatric Hospital, Medical Hospital, and Charter Schools (Excel Academy) programs report SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes and do not report SchoolDayOperationalMinutes.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
CalendarReference
The Calendar Reference is the identifier assigned to the Calendar.
Date (E1168) is the month, day, and year of the calendar date.
CalendarEvent (E1582) is the type of scheduled or unscheduled event for the day. For example: Instructional day or Waiver day.
For the PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4), when reporting the calendar dates for the ADSY Program, use CalendarEventDescriptor 01 (Instructional Day). Waivers do not apply to this program.
For additional guidance related to reporting calendar events for non-standard programs (JJAEP, DAEP, Prekindergarten, etc.), refer to the Special Reporting Requirements section.
CalendarWaiverEventType (E1570) indicates the type of state approved waiver.
SchoolDayOperationalMinutes (E1571) indicates the minutes that a campus operated on a particular school day for the purpose of student instruction.
SchoolDayOperationalMinutes is only reported for CalendarTypeDescriptors that are following 75,600 Operational Minutes.
SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes (E1599) indicates the portion of the school day in which instruction takes place along with certain other exceptions and are considered a subset of operational minutes.
SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes is only reported for CalendarTypeDescriptors that are not following 75,600 Operational Minutes or a 180-day school year calendar.
TEC §25.081(g) specifies that a school district may not provide student instruction on Memorial Day. If a school district would be required to provide student instruction on Memorial Day to compensate for minutes of instruction lost because of school closures caused by disaster, flood, extreme weather conditions, fuel curtailment, or another calamity, the commissioner shall approve the instruction of students for fewer than the minimum number of minutes required by TEC §25.081. A school must apply for a waiver(s) to exercise this option of the commissioner of education waving student instruction on Memorial Day.
SchoolDayWaiverMinutes (E1572) indicates the waiver minutes for the campus and calendar date.
Refer to the Calendar Waiver Scenarios table below for additional information about reporting waivers and school day minutes.

The collection of the data on the CalendarDate Entity is limited to the days that students are planned to attend school and the days that are sub-planted with a waiver and the students do not actually attend school either for a partial day or a full day. Do not report school holidays, such as spring break, weekends, or any other time that staff and students are not expected to be at school. Do not include staff work days that are not related to exercising the option of using a staff development waiver in lieu of a student instruction day.
Because schools that operate a CalendarType 01 (Standard Program 75,600 operation mins) are required to operate a school year consisting of at least 75,600 school day operational minutes, the sum of the SchoolDayOperationalMinutes and the SchoolDayWaiverMinutes should add to at least 75,600 minutes.
Each campus that reports at least one student in attendance during the course of the school year must also report school calendar data.
Per TEC 25.081(g) a school cannot plan on Memorial Day being an operational day or student school day when building the calendar(s) for a campus and then ask for the waiver.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
The CalendarDate Entity for the Optional Flexible School Day Program (OFSDP) Credit/Promotion Recovery Program, the Extended School Year Program, and the Additional Days School Year (ADSY) Program is reported in the PEIMS Extended Year Submission.
## GR3
Special Education Data System (SPEDS) - Summer Submission:
The CalendarDate Entity is used by the SPEDS - Summer Submission for students being evaluated for Special Education services (SPPI-11).
For all students reported for SPPI-11, the current year CalendarDate Entity and prior year PEIMS Summer Accepted calendar data may be used for TEA to calculate the following:
- The number of instructional days needed to complete the student’s evaluation once the LEA receives consent.
- The number of instructional days left in the school year beginning the first instructional day after parental consent was received.
- The last instructional day of the school year.
Additionally, for students reporting a ConsentToEvaluationReceivedDate in one school year and an EligibilityDeterminationDate in a different school year, the SPEDS - Summer Submission will use the student’s 15th day of school from the CalendarDate Entity (current) to calculate the Federal compliance information.

Special Requirements: ## SR1
Prekindergarten Programs (CalendarType 04, 14, or, 15):
Each prekindergarten program should be on its own CalendarCode.
Half-day Prekindergarten programs report SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes and do not report SchoolDayOperationalMinutes.
JJAEP (CalendarType 13):
JJAEPs report days of operation based on 180 days/7 hours a day, and do not report SchoolDayOperationalMinutes OR SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes. Waivers for JJAEPs are issued by the Texas Juvenile Justice Department (TJJD) and not TEA. JJAEPs should only use CalendarWaiverEventTypeDescriptor 05 (JJAEP School Day Waiver Issued by Texas Juvenile Justice Department (TJJD)).
Additional Days School Year Program (CalendarType 16)
When reporting the calendar dates for the ADSY Program, use CalendarEventDescriptor 01 (Instructional Day). Waivers do not apply to this program.
Other CalendarTypes:
Dropout Recovery, DAEP, Correctional Facility, Residential Treatment Facility, Day Treatment Facility, Psychiatric Hospital, Medical Hospital, and Charter Schools (Excel Academy) programs report SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes and do not report SchoolDayOperationalMinutes.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
CalendarReference
The Calendar Reference is the identifier assigned to the Calendar.
Date (E1168) is the month, day, and year of the calendar date.
CalendarEvent (E1582) is the type of scheduled or unscheduled event for the day. For example: Instructional day or Waiver day.
For the PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4), when reporting the calendar dates for the ADSY Program, use CalendarEventDescriptor 01 (Instructional Day). Waivers do not apply to this program.
For additional guidance related to reporting calendar events for non-standard programs (JJAEP, DAEP, Prekindergarten, etc.), refer to the Special Reporting Requirements section.
CalendarWaiverEventType (E1570) indicates the type of state approved waiver.
SchoolDayOperationalMinutes (E1571) indicates the minutes that a campus operated on a particular school day for the purpose of student instruction.
SchoolDayOperationalMinutes is only reported for CalendarTypeDescriptors that are following 75,600 Operational Minutes.
SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes (E1599) indicates the portion of the school day in which instruction takes place along with certain other exceptions and are considered a subset of operational minutes.
SchoolDayInstructionalMinutes is only reported for CalendarTypeDescriptors that are not following 75,600 Operational Minutes or a 180-day school year calendar.
TEC §25.081(g) specifies that a school district may not provide student instruction on Memorial Day. If a school district would be required to provide student instruction on Memorial Day to compensate for minutes of instruction lost because of school closures caused by disaster, flood, extreme weather conditions, fuel curtailment, or another calamity, the commissioner shall approve the instruction of students for fewer than the minimum number of minutes required by TEC §25.081. A school must apply for a waiver(s) to exercise this option of the commissioner of education waving student instruction on Memorial Day.
SchoolDayWaiverMinutes (E1572) indicates the waiver minutes for the campus and calendar date.
Refer to the Calendar Waiver Scenarios table below for additional information about reporting waivers and school day minutes.

=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
Yearly, the Texas Education Agency (TEA) will preload the Course Entity information into each local education entities (LEAs) individual operational data store (IODS). Only the State CourseCodes will be loaded by TEA.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
LocalEducationAgency Reference
The LocalEducationAgency Reference represents the identifier assigned to the Local Education Agency.
CourseCode (E3071) refers to a unique alphanumeric code assigned to a course.
CourseTitle (E3073) is the descriptive name given to a course of study offered in a school or other institution or organization.
NumberOfParts is required in the Ed-Fi model and is mandatory for the entity to be loaded into the individual operational data store (IODS). NumberOfParts will not be promoted to TSDS.
## DR2
Course>CourseIdentificationCode
The CourseIdentificationCode common type represents a standard code that identifies the organization of subject matter and related learning experiences provided for the instruction of students.
CourseIdentificationSystem (E3075) is the system that is used to identify the organization of subject matter and related learning experiences provided for the instruction of students.
The CourseIdentificationSystem for a LocalCourseCode (E1194) will be 02 (LEA Course Code). All other courses will be an 01 (State Course Code).
IdentificationCode (E3076) is a unique number of alphanumeric code assigned to a course or assessment by a school, school system, state, or other agency or entity.

=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
Yearly, the Texas Education Agency (TEA) will preload the Course Entity information into each local education entities (LEAs) individual operational data store (IODS). Only the State CourseCodes will be loaded by TEA.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
LocalEducationAgency Reference
The LocalEducationAgency Reference represents the identifier assigned to the Local Education Agency.
CourseCode (E3071) refers to a unique alphanumeric code assigned to a course.
CourseTitle (E3073) is the descriptive name given to a course of study offered in a school or other institution or organization.
NumberOfParts is required in the Ed-Fi model and is mandatory for the entity to be loaded into the individual operational data store (IODS). NumberOfParts will not be promoted to TSDS.
## DR2
Course>CourseIdentificationCode
The CourseIdentificationCode common type represents a standard code that identifies the organization of subject matter and related learning experiences provided for the instruction of students.
CourseIdentificationSystem (E3075) is the system that is used to identify the organization of subject matter and related learning experiences provided for the instruction of students.
The CourseIdentificationSystem for a LocalCourseCode (E1194) will be 02 (LEA Course Code). All other courses will be an 01 (State Course Code).
IdentificationCode (E3076) is a unique number of alphanumeric code assigned to a course or assessment by a school, school system, state, or other agency or entity.

elements.business_rules_text:
=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
The CourseTranscriptExt Entity is only reported for course sections from the StudentSectionAssociation entity where the CourseCompletionIndicator is true.
The CourseTranscriptExt Entity captures the completed course activity for students.
Local-credit courses such as the 8XXXXXXX series courses are not reported.
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
The CourseTranscriptExt Entity is reported for completed courses (CourseCompletionIndicator is true) for the current school year for:
- High school courses
If a student repeats and completes a course during the year with different outcomes, each course completion is to be reported.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
The CourseTranscriptExt Entity is reported for completed courses (CourseCompletionIndicator is true) during the summer (between school years) for:
- Career and Technical Education (CTE) courses,
- Dual credit courses,
- College Preparatory Course English Language Arts, or
- College Preparatory Course Mathematics.
Do not report the CourseTranscriptExt Entity for a course where the CourseCompletionIndicator is not true.

Special Requirements: ## SR1
AP Computer Science A
CourseTranscriptExt Entities must be reported for AP Computer Science A (LOTE – A3580120 and Math – A3580110) with the same CourseAttemptResult.
IB Computer Science Higher Level
CourseTranscriptExt Entities must be reported for IB Computer Science Higher Level (LOTE – I3580320 and Math – I3580310) with the same CourseAttemptResult.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
Course Reference
The Course Reference represents the identifier assigned to a course.
Section Reference
The Section Reference represents the identifier assigned to the section.
StudentAcademicRecord Reference
The StudentAcademicRecord Reference represents the identifier assigned to a student’s academic record.
CourseSequence (E0948) identifies the unique part(s) of a course when a course is taught during a single grading period or semester or across multiple grading periods or semesters.
The CourseSequence identifies how the course was taught to the student during the school year, or in the summer.  The CourseSequence identifies the order in which the course was scheduled in the class scheduling system. CourseSequence 1 (First Half Of A Two Semester Course) or D1 (First Half of a Two Semester Dual Credit Course) must be used for the first semester of a two-semester course, no matter if the course is taken in the fall or spring semester.
Dual credit CourseSequences are used for dual credit courses only. The length of the course for dual credit courses refers to the length of the college course, not the high school course.
CourseAttemptResult (E0949) indicates the outcome for a course taken by a particular student.
The CourseAttemptResult is only reported for courses where the CourseCompletionIndicator is true.
The CourseTranscript Entity must reflect the CourseAttemptResult determined at the end of the course.
Chemistry Example:
A student completes the first half of Chemistry, a two-semester course. The course was failed, no credit was received, CourseAttemptResult 02 (Course Was Failed No Credit Received – 1st Occurrence This School Year). The second semester, this student completed the second half of Chemistry. The course was passed, and credit was received, CourseAttemptResult 01 (Course Was Passed And Credit Was Received).  The district averages the grades earned in each half of the course to determine if course credit should be received. In this example, the average grade was passing. The CourseTranscript Entity should reflect a CourseAttemptResult 08 (Course Failed, Credit Rec (credit from grades in other parts of course)) for the first half of Chemistry. Therefore, the CourseAttemptResult 02 (Course Was Failed No Credit Received – 1st Occurrence This School Year) originally recorded must be changed to CourseAttemptResult 08 (Course Failed, Credit Rec (credit from grades in other parts of course)).
For dual credit courses, CourseAttemptResult must reflects the high school outcome for the course taken, not the college outcome.
EarnedCredits is required in the Ed-Fi model and is mandatory for the entity to be loaded into the individual operational data store (IODS). EarnedCredits will not be promoted to TSDS.
CollegeCreditHours (E1081) indicate the number of college hours a student earned for the completion of a dual credit course.
If a student completes a dual credit course and does not pass the course, then the CollegeCreditHours will be reported as 0.
If a student completes an OnRamps Dual Enrollment course and does not pass the course, then the CollegeCreditHours will be reported as 0.
When a course is reported as eligible to receive dual credit, be cautious to avoid duplicating the college credit hours earned across multiple course sections. College credit hours should only be reported when a student completes and passes a one semester course (CourseSequence D0 (Single Semester Dual Credit Course)) or the last part of a multi-part course (CourseSequence D2 (Second Half of a Two Semester Dual Credit Course), D5 (Last Third of a Three Semester Dual Credit Course), or D9 (Last Fourth of a Four Semester Dual Credit Course)).
Note: CollegeCreditHours are only reported for students who earn college credit hours for a Dual Credit or OnRamps course. For OnRamps courses, this information may be found on a student’s individual UT Austin OnRamps transcript or reports received from UT Austin OnRamps regarding the student’s progress in the course.
DualCreditIndicator (E1011) indicates whether the student was eligible to receive both high school and college credit for a college course.
Advanced Placement courses reported on the StudentAcademicRecord Entity cannot be reported as dual credit unless the course has been approved as an AP® course by the College Board through the AP® Course Audit. A College Board-approved AP® course must adhere to the AP® course descriptions and be approved through the AP® Course Audit. This means the college instructor must have submitted their course syllabus and have received approval in advance.
Note: Do not report DualCreditIndicator for students who complete an OnRamps course through the University of Texas at Austin.
SummerSchoolIndicator (E3091) indicates the course completed by a student was completed during the summer (between school years).
DropoutRecoveryCourseCompletion (E3097) indicates if the course completed by a student in a dropout recovery education program under TEC §29.081 was completed in person or remotely.
OnRampsDualEnrollmentIndicator (E3120) indicates that the student has completed an OnRamps dual enrollment course.
OnRamps is an innovative dual enrollment program coordinated by the University of Texas at Austin (reported in Submissions 3 and 4 only).
OnRamps courses cannot be reported with the DualCreditIndicator.
Note: CollegeCreditHours are only reported for students who earn college credit hours for the OnRamps course. This information may be found on a student’s individual UT Austin OnRamps transcript or reports received from UT Austin OnRamps regarding the student’s progress in the course.

=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
Disciplinary actions that result in the removal of a student from any part of their regular academic program will be reported as: In-School Suspension (ISS), Out-of-School Suspension (OSS), Expulsion, Juvenile Justice Alternative Education Program (JJAEP) assignment, or DAEP assignment. Refer to PEIMS descriptor table Discipline (C164) for the specific actions to be reported.
For JJAEP, DAEP, and Expulsion assignments that involve any part of a day:
- The OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment fields should be rounded up to the next whole number.  

For example, a student is assigned to DAEP for three days and begins their DAEP placement in the middle of the school day. Although the student will only be in DAEP for 2.5 days, the discipline record will be reported with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of three days.
- For example, a student is assigned to DAEP for three days and begins their DAEP placement in the middle of the school day. Although the student will only be in DAEP for 2.5 days, the discipline record will be reported with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of three days.
For ISS and OSS:
- Any removal of the student for a partial day will be reported as a whole day with a value of 1 (one) in the OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment fields.
- If the removal is for a partial day, then Discipline 25 (Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspension) or 26 (Partial Day In-School Suspension) will be used to reflect the partial day assignments to either ISS or OSS.
- This also applies to consecutive or non-consecutive partial day assignments where the assignment is for more than one calendar day.

For example, a student is assigned OSS for 2.5 days and begins the assignment in the middle of the school day. The student will be suspended for 2.5 days. There will be two discipline records reported:

Report Discipline code 25 (Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspension) for the half day, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of one day, and
Also report Discipline code 05 (Out-Of-School Suspension) for the remaining 2 days, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of two days.
- For example, a student is assigned OSS for 2.5 days and begins the assignment in the middle of the school day. The student will be suspended for 2.5 days. There will be two discipline records reported:

Report Discipline code 25 (Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspension) for the half day, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of one day, and
Also report Discipline code 05 (Out-Of-School Suspension) for the remaining 2 days, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of two days.

- Also report Discipline code 05 (Out-Of-School Suspension) for the remaining 2 days, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of two days.
OSS under TEC, §37.005, may not exceed three school days. (TEC, §37.005(b))
For JJAEP:
- An LEA will report each disciplinary action that results in the removal of a student from any part of their regular academic program, including a placement or continuation of a placement in a JJAEP, with the DisciplineAction entity. Applicable Discipline codes are 02 (Expulsion With Placement In A JJAEP), 12 (Continuation Of District’s Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year), 13 (Placement In A JJAEP By Court Order), 15 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP), 51 (Expulsion With Placement To A JJAEP – SPED), 59 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year – SPED), 60 (Placement In A JJAEP – SPED), and 61 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP – SPED).
- An LEA will not report any disciplinary actions taken by the JJAEP school administration.
For DAEP’s or Shared Service Arrangements for DAEP services or participating in a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for JJAEP’s:
- All days of operation for student attendance must be reported through PEIMS Summer Submission (3).
- There is no Summer School Program period for disciplinary programs such as DAEPs or JJAEPs and all days of student attendance for disciplinary assignments must be reported through PEIMS Summer Submission (3). The decision to accept days attended during summer school for attended days in DAEP is determined by local policy.
- Each district has control over when its district's calendar for a DAEP or JJAEP begins and ends.  

For example, if the JJAEP has a 220-day calendar, and a school district’s traditional calendar runs from August 15, 20YY through May 30, 20XY, then the calendar for the JJAEP could potentially run from June 1, 20YY through May 30, 20XY or some variation such that the district’s ability to report data for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) by the required due dates is not impaired.

## GR2
The PEIMS Chart for Determining Mandatory and Disciplinary DAEP Placements and Expulsions illustrates those occasions where mandatory action(s) must be taken.  If the offense committed falls under either Mandatory DAEP Placement or Mandatory Expulsion, then the district should report at least one (1) Student Disciplinary Action that matches the chart. Appropriate exceptions would include students receiving special education services for whom a manifestation ARD was held in accordance with the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), and it was determined a link existed between the student’s behavior and the student’s disability. Reporting such an exception, the district must submit one DisciplinaryAction with Discipline code 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee) and another DisciplinaryAction(s) with the Discipline code(s) that were taken by the district using the same incident number linking the records together.
Another exception is when a school district determines that the mandatory disciplinary action will not be taken because the district considered one or more of the TEC, §37.001(a)(4) provisions that requires the district to consider self-defense, intent or lack of intent, student’s disciplinary history, disability that substantially impairs the student’s capacity to appreciate the wrongfulness of the student’s conduct, a student's status in the conservatorship of the Department of Family and Protective Services, or a student's status as a student who is homeless as a factor in a decision to order suspension, (including ISS and OSS), removal to a disciplinary alternative education program, or expulsion. The district must submit one DisciplinaryAction with Discipline code 28 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - TEC 37.001(a)(4)) and another DisciplinaryAction(s) with the Discipline code(s) of the action(s) that were taken by the district using the same incident number linking the records together.
For the behaviors identified in TEC §37.006, refer to the “Mandatory DAEP Placement” column on the Chart for Determining Mandatory Placement and Expulsion Codes:
- For students identified with one of these behaviors there must be a DisciplineAction entity illustrating at least one day of removal to a DAEP unless the student is a student receiving special education services for whom a manifestation hearing is held in accordance with IDEA and a determination made that the mandatory action is not appropriate and will not be taken.
- When the mandatory action is not taken and another action is taken, the district must submit a DisciplineAction entity with Discipline 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee) and a DisciplineAction entity with the action(s) taken by the district. Both entities must have the same Discipline.
For the behaviors identified in TEC §37.007, refer to the “Mandatory Expulsion” column on the Chart for Determining Mandatory Placement and Expulsion Codes:
- For students identified with one of these behaviors there must be a DisciplineAction entity illustrating at least one day of expulsion to either a JJAEP, DAEP, no academic setting, or Virtual Expulsion Program based upon the requirements in state law and/or district policy unless the student is a student receiving special education services for whom a manifestation hearing is held in accordance with IDEA and a determination made that the mandatory action is not appropriate and will not be taken.
- When the mandatory action is not taken and another action is taken, the district must submit a DisciplineAction entity with Discipline code 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee) and a DisciplineAction entity with the action(s) taken by the district.  Both entities must have the same Discipline code.
- Except for the reason of “bringing a firearm to school,” a student who is younger than 10 years of age may not be expelled for engaging in conduct described in TEC 37.007. Students who are less than 10 years of age and commit an otherwise expellable offense must be placed in a DAEP via a DAEP conference hearing in lieu of an expulsion hearing. Students under the age of 10 who bring a firearm to school must be expelled with placement to a DAEP.
## GR3
Discipline over multiple years:
Anytime a disciplinary action continues over multiple school years or multiple school districts, the reporting period indicator code for continuation assignments should be the reporting period in which the continuation assignment is made in the subsequent school year or by the subsequent school district.  Be sure that continuation Discipline codes 08 (Continuation Of Other District’s DAEP Placement), 09 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion Order ), 10 (Continuation Of District’s DAEP Placement From Prior School Year), 11 (Continuation Of District’s Expulsion Order From Prior School Year), 12 (Continuation Of District’s Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year), 15 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP), 55 (Continuation Of Other District’s DAEP Placement – SPED), 56 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion Order – SPED), 57 (Continuation Of District's DAEP Placement From Prior School Year – SPED), 58 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion Order From Prior School Year – SPED), 59 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year – SPED), or 61 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP - SPED ) are used when continuing a disciplinary assignment from a prior year or prior district.
A single incident/offense may result in multiple disciplinary actions. In such cases, multiple DisciplineAction records must be reported for each action taken against a particular student for a particular incident/offense. See Example EX1.
If a student is involved in a reportable disciplinary incident, and the student attempts to withdraw from school before the disciplinary assignment is made, the district/school should complete the due-process proceedings that result in a disciplinary assignment before the student is allowed to withdraw and then the district is required to report the discipline record reflecting that assignment in order to remain in compliance with TEC §37.009.
Whenever a student is reported with multiple discipline records at the same CampusIDOfEnrollment, at least one of the elements IncidentIdentifier, Discipline, or DisciplineDate must be different. An exception to this rule would be an instance where the teacher has permanently removed a student from their classroom (Discipline code 01 (Expulsion Without Placement In Another Educational Setting)) and the campus administrator has no other academic setting available for the student for this particular time period/subject.
The use of Discipline codes "50"-"61" are limited to those occasions when a Special Education hearing officer assigned by the TEA has been brought in to preside over the Discipline Action Hearing.
If a Discipline code is 50 (Expulsion Without Placement In Another Educational Setting - SPED), 51 (Expulsion With Placement To A JJAEP - SPED), 52 (Expulsion With Placement To An On-Campus DAEP - SPED), 53 (Expulsion With Placement To An Off-Campus DAEP - SPED), 54 (Placement In An On-Campus Or Off-Campus DAEP - SPED ), 55 (Continuation Of Other District’s DAEP Placement – SPED), 56 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion Order – SPED), 57 (Continuation Of District's DAEP Placement From Prior School Year – SPED), 58 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion Order From Prior School Year – SPED), 59 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year – SPED), 60 (Placement In A JJAEP - SPED), or 61 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP - SPED ) then there should be at least some Regular or Flexible Special Education Attendance reported for this student in the same reporting period, unless the student lives out-of-state and is not eligible for ADA funding.
If a Discipline code is 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee), then there should be at least some Regular or Flexible Special Education Attendance reported for this student in the same reporting period, unless the student lives out-of-state and is not eligible for ADA funding.
A student should not have more disciplinary removals in a six-week reporting period than there are days in membership (sum of TotalEligibleDaysPresent, TotalIneligibleDaysPresent and TotalDaysAbsent) on the Basic Attendance data for that student during that same reporting period.
A student should not have more than one day of disciplinary removal assigned or served for Discipline codes 25 (Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspension) or 26 (Partial Day In-School Suspension). For Partial Day In-School Suspensions or Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspensions, the OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment should not be greater than one (1) day, unless it is a Permanent Removal By a Teacher from Class (Discipline code 01 (Expulsion Without Placement In Another Educational Setting)). Disciplinary removal assignments to Out-Of-School Suspension or In-School Suspension that are greater than one day should generally be reported with Discipline codes 05 (Out-Of-School Suspension) or 06 (In-School Suspension).
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
If a special education student is enrolled but not in membership and the special education student has a discipline incident, the DisciplineAction entity shall be reported.

Special Requirements: ## SR1
For disciplinary removals of a student who is receiving special education and related services from the student's current educational placement, a change of placement occurs if the removal is for more than ten consecutive days (CFR §300.530 - §300.536). The ARD committee that deals with the change of placement must review the student's IEP to detail the special education and related services to be administered to the student while he is removed for discipline reasons. Be careful not to confuse the 10-day change of placement requirement for special education purposes with the 1-day removal requirement for discipline record reporting purposes. A discipline record is required for all students who are receiving special education and related services and are removed from their regularly scheduled classes for one day or more.  A change of placement occurs when the removal is for more than ten consecutive days, and a change of placement may occur when the removal is for more than ten current or cumulative days in a school year based on factors such as the length of each removal, the total amount of the time the child is removed, and the proximity of the removals to one another. An ARD committee must be involved when the removal or series of removals constitutes a change in placement.
DAEPs and JJAEPs
For LEAs operating DAEPs, or participating in Shared Service Arrangements for DAEP services, or participating in a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for JJAEPs, all days of operation for student attendance must be reported through PEIMS Summer Submission (3).  There is no Summer School Program period for disciplinary programs such as DAEPs or JJAEPs and all days of student attendance for disciplinary assignments must be reported through PEIMS Summer Submission (3).  The decision to accept days attended during summer school for attended days in DAEP is determined by local policy. A district still has control over when the district's calendar for a DAEP or JJAEP begins and ends so long as all days of student operation are reported. For example, if the JJAEP has a 220-day calendar, and a school district’s traditional calendar runs from August 15, 20XX through May 30, 20YY, then the calendar for the JJAEP would potentially run from June 1, 20XX through May 30, 20YY or some variation such that the district’s ability to report data for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) is not inconveniently impaired.
In order to place a student in a JJAEP or DAEP by a Court order, there must be a MOU between the court ordering the placement and the school district that will affect and make the placement.  In all circumstances of court ordered placements to a JJAEP or DAEP, the Behavior code must be a 21 (Violation of student code of conduct not included under TEC §§37.002(b), 37.006, or 37.007).
In the event that a school district finds it necessary to continue a Court ordered placement to a JJAEP or a DAEP from a prior school year or a prior school district, a new discipline record must be reported with a Behavior code 21 (Violation of student code of conduct not included under TEC §§37.002(b), 37.006, or 37.007) and a Discipline code 13 (Placement In A JJAEP By Court Order) or 14 (Placement In A DAEP By Court Order) depending on the action taken.  Remember that DAEP assignments that continue into a new school year are subject to the requirements of TEC 37.009(c) referenced in the PEIMS Discipline Data guidance.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
Student Reference
The Student Reference represents the identifier assigned to a student.
StudentDisciplineIncidentBehaviorAssociation Reference
The StudentDisciplineIncidentBehaviorAssociation Reference represents the behavior by the student that led or contributed to this specific action.
AssignmentSchool (E1003) indicates the unique campus identification number of the campus in which the student was placed for disciplinary reasons.
ResponsibilitySchool (E1037) indicates the instructional campus on which the student was enrolled when the student code of conduct was fractured and the disciplinary assignment was made, or for a continuation disciplinary assignment the campus that the student would attend under all normal circumstances if not under a disciplinary assignment.
DisciplineActionIdentifier (E1004) indicates the differentiation between two or more separate disciplinary actions reported with identical values for StudentId and CampusIdOfEnrollment.
DisciplineActionIdentifier is used to differentiate between separate disciplinary actions for a particular student on a particular campus. For example, while Janice was enrolled on Campus 002, she had DisciplineActionIdentifier codes 001-013 reported on her discipline records for Campus 002. After Janice moved to Campus 005, she had DisciplineActionIdentifier codes 001-004 reported on her discipline records for Campus 005. However, districts/campuses may choose any numbering sequence, as long as the same number is not repeated for a particular student at a particular campus.
DisciplineDate (E1036) indicates the instructional date on which the disciplinary assignment was ordered. This may or may not reflect the date on which the disciplinary infraction occurred. This date may or may not reflect the date on which the disciplinary assignment begins. For continuation assignments, this date reflects the first instructional day of the continuation.
The date range for the DisciplineDate is from July 1 through June 30 of each reporting year.
ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment (E1008) indicates the actual length in days of a student’s disciplinary assignment.
Include only the actual number of instructional school days that the student was in attendance when calculating this number. Do not include days absent. Round up to the nearest whole number.
Discipline (E1005) indicates the type of disciplinary action taken for a student.
The Discipline data element can have multiple instances.
OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment (E1007) indicates the official length in days of a student’s disciplinary assignment.
Round up to the nearest whole number.
DisciplineActionLengthDifferenceReason (E1009) indicates the reason for the difference, if any, between the official and actual lengths of a student’s disciplinary assignment.
InconsistentCodeOfConduct (E1656) indicates whether an out-of-school suspension (OSS), disciplinary alternative education program (DAEP) placement (not by court order), or expulsion action is inconsistent with a local education agency’s student code of conduct.
For DAEP placements and expulsions, §37.020 of the Texas Education Code (TEC) requires that any DAEP placement or expulsion, whether mandatory or discretionary, with a length of term inconsistent with the guidelines included in the student code of conduct under §37.001(a)(5) of the Texas Education Code be reported.
For OSS, TEC §37.020 requires that a suspension inconsistent with the guidelines included in the student code of conduct under TEC §37.001(a)(3) outlining conditions under which a student may be suspended as provided by §37.005 be reported.
## DR2
InconsistentCodeOfConduct (E1656) is only required when the Discipline (E1005) is an OSS, DAEP placement, or expulsion.

- When the mandatory action is not taken and another action is taken, the district must submit a DisciplineAction entity with Discipline 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee) and a DisciplineAction entity with the action(s) taken by the district. Both entities must have the same Discipline.
For the behaviors identified in TEC §37.007, refer to the “Mandatory Expulsion” column on the Chart for Determining Mandatory Placement and Expulsion Codes:
- For students identified with one of these behaviors there must be a DisciplineAction entity illustrating at least one day of expulsion to either a JJAEP, DAEP, no academic setting, or Virtual Expulsion Program based upon the requirements in state law and/or district policy unless the student is a student receiving special education services for whom a manifestation hearing is held in accordance with IDEA and a determination made that the mandatory action is not appropriate and will not be taken.

- Except for the reason of “bringing a firearm to school,” a student who is younger than 10 years of age may not be expelled for engaging in conduct described in TEC 37.007. Students who are less than 10 years of age and commit an otherwise expellable offense must be placed in a DAEP via a DAEP conference hearing in lieu of an expulsion hearing. Students under the age of 10 who bring a firearm to school must be expelled with placement to a DAEP.

A single incident/offense may result in multiple disciplinary actions. In such cases, multiple DisciplineAction records must be reported for each action taken against a particular student for a particular incident/offense. See Example EX1.

If a Discipline code is 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee), then there should be at least some Regular or Flexible Special Education Attendance reported for this student in the same reporting period, unless the student lives out-of-state and is not eligible for ADA funding.

Special Requirements: ## SR1
For disciplinary removals of a student who is receiving special education and related services from the student's current educational placement, a change of placement occurs if the removal is for more than ten consecutive days (CFR §300.530 - §300.536). A discipline record is required for all students who are receiving special education and related services and are removed from their regularly scheduled classes for one day or more.  A change of placement occurs when the removal is for more than ten consecutive days, and a change of placement may occur when the removal is for more than ten current or cumulative days in a school year based on factors such as the length of each removal, the total amount of the time the child is removed, and the proximity of the removals to one another. An ARD committee must be involved when the removal or series of removals constitutes a change in placement.
DAEPs and JJAEPs
For LEAs operating DAEPs, or participating in Shared Service Arrangements for DAEP services, or participating in a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for JJAEPs, all days of operation for student attendance must be reported through PEIMS Summer Submission (3).  There is no Summer School Program period for disciplinary programs such as DAEPs or JJAEPs and all days of student attendance for disciplinary assignments must be reported through PEIMS Summer Submission (3).  The decision to accept days attended during summer school for attended days in DAEP is determined by local policy. A district still has control over when the district's calendar for a DAEP or JJAEP begins and ends so long as all days of student operation are reported. For example, if the JJAEP has a 220-day calendar, and a school district’s traditional calendar runs from August 15, 20XX through May 30, 20YY, then the calendar for the JJAEP would potentially run from June 1, 20XX through May 30, 20YY or some variation such that the district’s ability to report data for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) is not inconveniently impaired.

Student Reference
The Student Reference represents the identifier assigned to a student.
StudentDisciplineIncidentBehaviorAssociation Reference
The StudentDisciplineIncidentBehaviorAssociation Reference represents the behavior by the student that led or contributed to this specific action.
AssignmentSchool (E1003) indicates the unique campus identification number of the campus in which the student was placed for disciplinary reasons.
ResponsibilitySchool (E1037) indicates the instructional campus on which the student was enrolled when the student code of conduct was fractured and the disciplinary assignment was made, or for a continuation disciplinary assignment the campus that the student would attend under all normal circumstances if not under a disciplinary assignment.
DisciplineActionIdentifier (E1004) indicates the differentiation between two or more separate disciplinary actions reported with identical values for StudentId and CampusIdOfEnrollment.
DisciplineActionIdentifier is used to differentiate between separate disciplinary actions for a particular student on a particular campus. For example, while Janice was enrolled on Campus 002, she had DisciplineActionIdentifier codes 001-013 reported on her discipline records for Campus 002. After Janice moved to Campus 005, she had DisciplineActionIdentifier codes 001-004 reported on her discipline records for Campus 005. However, districts/campuses may choose any numbering sequence, as long as the same number is not repeated for a particular student at a particular campus.
DisciplineDate (E1036) indicates the instructional date on which the disciplinary assignment was ordered. This may or may not reflect the date on which the disciplinary infraction occurred. This date may or may not reflect the date on which the disciplinary assignment begins. For continuation assignments, this date reflects the first instructional day of the continuation.
The date range for the DisciplineDate is from July 1 through June 30 of each reporting year.
ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment (E1008) indicates the actual length in days of a student’s disciplinary assignment.
Include only the actual number of instructional school days that the student was in attendance when calculating this number. Do not include days absent. Round up to the nearest whole number.
Discipline (E1005) indicates the type of disciplinary action taken for a student.
The Discipline data element can have multiple instances.
OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment (E1007) indicates the official length in days of a student’s disciplinary assignment.
Round up to the nearest whole number.
DisciplineActionLengthDifferenceReason (E1009) indicates the reason for the difference, if any, between the official and actual lengths of a student’s disciplinary assignment.

InconsistentCodeOfConduct (E1656) is only required when the Discipline (E1005) is an OSS, DAEP placement, or expulsion.

A discipline record is required for all students who are receiving special education and related services and are removed from their regularly scheduled classes for one day or more.  A change of placement occurs when the removal is for more than ten consecutive days, and a change of placement may occur when the removal is for more than ten current or cumulative days in a school year based on factors such as the length of each removal, the total amount of the time the child is removed, and the proximity of the removals to one another. An ARD committee must be involved when the removal or series of removals constitutes a change in placement.

For LEAs operating DAEPs, or participating in Shared Service Arrangements for DAEP services, or participating in a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for JJAEPs, all days of operation for student attendance must be reported through PEIMS Summer Submission (3).  There is no Summer School Program period for disciplinary programs such as DAEPs or JJAEPs and all days of student attendance for disciplinary assignments must be reported through PEIMS Summer Submission (3).  The decision to accept days attended during summer school for attended days in DAEP is determined by local policy. A district still has control over when the district's calendar for a DAEP or JJAEP begins and ends so long as all days of student operation are reported. For example, if the JJAEP has a 220-day calendar, and a school district’s traditional calendar runs from August 15, 20XX through May 30, 20YY, then the calendar for the JJAEP would potentially run from June 1, 20XX through May 30, 20YY or some variation such that the district’s ability to report data for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) is not inconveniently impaired.
In order to place a student in a JJAEP or DAEP by a Court order, there must be a MOU between the court ordering the placement and the school district that will affect and make the placement.  In all circumstances of court ordered placements to a JJAEP or DAEP, the Behavior code must be a 21 (Violation of student code of conduct not included under TEC §§37.002(b), 37.006, or 37.007).

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
Student Reference
The Student Reference represents the identifier assigned to a student.
StudentDisciplineIncidentBehaviorAssociation Reference
The StudentDisciplineIncidentBehaviorAssociation Reference represents the behavior by the student that led or contributed to this specific action.
AssignmentSchool (E1003) indicates the unique campus identification number of the campus in which the student was placed for disciplinary reasons.
ResponsibilitySchool (E1037) indicates the instructional campus on which the student was enrolled when the student code of conduct was fractured and the disciplinary assignment was made, or for a continuation disciplinary assignment the campus that the student would attend under all normal circumstances if not under a disciplinary assignment.
DisciplineActionIdentifier (E1004) indicates the differentiation between two or more separate disciplinary actions reported with identical values for StudentId and CampusIdOfEnrollment.

General Requirements: ## GR1
Disciplinary actions that result in the removal of a student from any part of their regular academic program will be reported as: In-School Suspension (ISS), Out-of-School Suspension (OSS), Expulsion, Juvenile Justice Alternative Education Program (JJAEP) assignment, or DAEP assignment. Refer to PEIMS descriptor table Discipline (C164) for the specific actions to be reported.
For JJAEP, DAEP, and Expulsion assignments that involve any part of a day:
- The OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment fields should be rounded up to the next whole number.  

For example, a student is assigned to DAEP for three days and begins their DAEP placement in the middle of the school day. Although the student will only be in DAEP for 2.5 days, the discipline record will be reported with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of three days.
- For example, a student is assigned to DAEP for three days and begins their DAEP placement in the middle of the school day. Although the student will only be in DAEP for 2.5 days, the discipline record will be reported with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of three days.
For ISS and OSS:
- Any removal of the student for a partial day will be reported as a whole day with a value of 1 (one) in the OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment fields.
- If the removal is for a partial day, then Discipline 25 (Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspension) or 26 (Partial Day In-School Suspension) will be used to reflect the partial day assignments to either ISS or OSS.
- This also applies to consecutive or non-consecutive partial day assignments where the assignment is for more than one calendar day.

For example, a student is assigned OSS for 2.5 days and begins the assignment in the middle of the school day. The student will be suspended for 2.5 days. There will be two discipline records reported:

Report Discipline code 25 (Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspension) for the half day, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of one day, and
Also report Discipline code 05 (Out-Of-School Suspension) for the remaining 2 days, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of two days.
- For example, a student is assigned OSS for 2.5 days and begins the assignment in the middle of the school day. The student will be suspended for 2.5 days. There will be two discipline records reported:

Report Discipline code 25 (Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspension) for the half day, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of one day, and
Also report Discipline code 05 (Out-Of-School Suspension) for the remaining 2 days, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of two days.
- Report Discipline code 25 (Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspension) for the half day, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of one day, and
- Also report Discipline code 05 (Out-Of-School Suspension) for the remaining 2 days, with OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment of two days.
OSS under TEC, §37.005, may not exceed three school days. (TEC, §37.005(b))
For JJAEP:
- An LEA will report each disciplinary action that results in the removal of a student from any part of their regular academic program, including a placement or continuation of a placement in a JJAEP, with the DisciplineAction entity. Applicable Discipline codes are 02 (Expulsion With Placement In A JJAEP), 12 (Continuation Of District’s Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year), 13 (Placement In A JJAEP By Court Order), 15 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP), 51 (Expulsion With Placement To A JJAEP – SPED), 59 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year – SPED), 60 (Placement In A JJAEP – SPED), and 61 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP – SPED).
- An LEA will not report any disciplinary actions taken by the JJAEP school administration.

## GR2
The PEIMS Chart for Determining Mandatory and Disciplinary DAEP Placements and Expulsions illustrates those occasions where mandatory action(s) must be taken.  If the offense committed falls under either Mandatory DAEP Placement or Mandatory Expulsion, then the district should report at least one (1) Student Disciplinary Action that matches the chart. Appropriate exceptions would include students receiving special education services for whom a manifestation ARD was held in accordance with the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), and it was determined a link existed between the student’s behavior and the student’s disability. Reporting such an exception, the district must submit one DisciplinaryAction with Discipline code 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee) and another DisciplinaryAction(s) with the Discipline code(s) that were taken by the district using the same incident number linking the records together.
Another exception is when a school district determines that the mandatory disciplinary action will not be taken because the district considered one or more of the TEC, §37.001(a)(4) provisions that requires the district to consider self-defense, intent or lack of intent, student’s disciplinary history, disability that substantially impairs the student’s capacity to appreciate the wrongfulness of the student’s conduct, a student's status in the conservatorship of the Department of Family and Protective Services, or a student's status as a student who is homeless as a factor in a decision to order suspension, (including ISS and OSS), removal to a disciplinary alternative education program, or expulsion. The district must submit one DisciplinaryAction with Discipline code 28 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - TEC 37.001(a)(4)) and another DisciplinaryAction(s) with the Discipline code(s) of the action(s) that were taken by the district using the same incident number linking the records together.
For the behaviors identified in TEC §37.006, refer to the “Mandatory DAEP Placement” column on the Chart for Determining Mandatory Placement and Expulsion Codes:
- For students identified with one of these behaviors there must be a DisciplineAction entity illustrating at least one day of removal to a DAEP unless the student is a student receiving special education services for whom a manifestation hearing is held in accordance with IDEA and a determination made that the mandatory action is not appropriate and will not be taken.
- When the mandatory action is not taken and another action is taken, the district must submit a DisciplineAction entity with Discipline 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee) and a DisciplineAction entity with the action(s) taken by the district. Both entities must have the same Discipline.
For the behaviors identified in TEC §37.007, refer to the “Mandatory Expulsion” column on the Chart for Determining Mandatory Placement and Expulsion Codes:
- For students identified with one of these behaviors there must be a DisciplineAction entity illustrating at least one day of expulsion to either a JJAEP, DAEP, no academic setting, or Virtual Expulsion Program based upon the requirements in state law and/or district policy unless the student is a student receiving special education services for whom a manifestation hearing is held in accordance with IDEA and a determination made that the mandatory action is not appropriate and will not be taken.
- When the mandatory action is not taken and another action is taken, the district must submit a DisciplineAction entity with Discipline code 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee) and a DisciplineAction entity with the action(s) taken by the district.  Both entities must have the same Discipline code.
- Except for the reason of “bringing a firearm to school,” a student who is younger than 10 years of age may not be expelled for engaging in conduct described in TEC 37.007. Students who are less than 10 years of age and commit an otherwise expellable offense must be placed in a DAEP via a DAEP conference hearing in lieu of an expulsion hearing. Students under the age of 10 who bring a firearm to school must be expelled with placement to a DAEP.
## GR3
Discipline over multiple years:
Anytime a disciplinary action continues over multiple school years or multiple school districts, the reporting period indicator code for continuation assignments should be the reporting period in which the continuation assignment is made in the subsequent school year or by the subsequent school district.  Be sure that continuation Discipline codes 08 (Continuation Of Other District’s DAEP Placement), 09 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion Order ), 10 (Continuation Of District’s DAEP Placement From Prior School Year), 11 (Continuation Of District’s Expulsion Order From Prior School Year), 12 (Continuation Of District’s Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year), 15 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP), 55 (Continuation Of Other District’s DAEP Placement – SPED), 56 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion Order – SPED), 57 (Continuation Of District's DAEP Placement From Prior School Year – SPED), 58 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion Order From Prior School Year – SPED), 59 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year – SPED), or 61 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP - SPED ) are used when continuing a disciplinary assignment from a prior year or prior district.
A single incident/offense may result in multiple disciplinary actions. In such cases, multiple DisciplineAction records must be reported for each action taken against a particular student for a particular incident/offense. See Example EX1.
If a student is involved in a reportable disciplinary incident, and the student attempts to withdraw from school before the disciplinary assignment is made, the district/school should complete the due-process proceedings that result in a disciplinary assignment before the student is allowed to withdraw and then the district is required to report the discipline record reflecting that assignment in order to remain in compliance with TEC §37.009.
Whenever a student is reported with multiple discipline records at the same CampusIDOfEnrollment, at least one of the elements IncidentIdentifier, Discipline, or DisciplineDate must be different. An exception to this rule would be an instance where the teacher has permanently removed a student from their classroom (Discipline code 01 (Expulsion Without Placement In Another Educational Setting)) and the campus administrator has no other academic setting available for the student for this particular time period/subject.
The use of Discipline codes "50"-"61" are limited to those occasions when a Special Education hearing officer assigned by the TEA has been brought in to preside over the Discipline Action Hearing.
If a Discipline code is 50 (Expulsion Without Placement In Another Educational Setting - SPED), 51 (Expulsion With Placement To A JJAEP - SPED), 52 (Expulsion With Placement To An On-Campus DAEP - SPED), 53 (Expulsion With Placement To An Off-Campus DAEP - SPED), 54 (Placement In An On-Campus Or Off-Campus DAEP - SPED ), 55 (Continuation Of Other District’s DAEP Placement – SPED), 56 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion Order – SPED), 57 (Continuation Of District's DAEP Placement From Prior School Year – SPED), 58 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion Order From Prior School Year – SPED), 59 (Continuation Of District's Expulsion To JJAEP From Prior School Year – SPED), 60 (Placement In A JJAEP - SPED), or 61 (Continuation Of Other District’s Expulsion With Placement To JJAEP - SPED ) then there should be at least some Regular or Flexible Special Education Attendance reported for this student in the same reporting period, unless the student lives out-of-state and is not eligible for ADA funding.
If a Discipline code is 27 (Mandatory Disciplinary Action Not Taken By District - ARD committee), then there should be at least some Regular or Flexible Special Education Attendance reported for this student in the same reporting period, unless the student lives out-of-state and is not eligible for ADA funding.
A student should not have more disciplinary removals in a six-week reporting period than there are days in membership (sum of TotalEligibleDaysPresent, TotalIneligibleDaysPresent and TotalDaysAbsent) on the Basic Attendance data for that student during that same reporting period.
A student should not have more than one day of disciplinary removal assigned or served for Discipline codes 25 (Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspension) or 26 (Partial Day In-School Suspension). For Partial Day In-School Suspensions or Partial Day Out-Of-School Suspensions, the OfficialLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment and ActualLengthOfDisciplinaryAssignment should not be greater than one (1) day, unless it is a Permanent Removal By a Teacher from Class (Discipline code 01 (Expulsion Without Placement In Another Educational Setting)). Disciplinary removal assignments to Out-Of-School Suspension or In-School Suspension that are greater than one day should generally be reported with Discipline codes 05 (Out-Of-School Suspension) or 06 (In-School Suspension).

elements.business_rules_text:
=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
Report a DisciplineIncident Entity for each occurrence of an infraction.
Discipline records are reported at the end of the current school year and are a part of the PEIMS Summer Submission (3).
Discipline record data is required by TEC, Chapter 37, P.L. 114-95 - Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA), and IDEA 2004, which includes students who are receiving special education and related services. TEA will maintain the privacy of this personally identifiable information in accordance with FERPA.
For purposes of discipline data reported to TEA, the attendance/PEIMS data personnel are only responsible for entering information that has been provided to them by the Superintendent or their designee(s) who are responsible for applying the Student Code of Conduct to student behavior.  In no case should attendance/PEIMS data personnel be responsible for determining a student's coding information for discipline actions taken.
A PEIMS DisciplineIncident Entity must be reported for each disciplinary action that results in a removal of a student from any part of their regular academic program as required by TEC, §37.020.  A single student will have multiple discipline records if removed from his classroom more than once.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
School Reference
The School Reference represents the identifier assigned to a school.
IncidentIdentifier (E1016) designates an incident that occurs on a campus and results in one or more disciplinary actions for one or more students.
If, on a single campus, more than one student is involved in an incident that results in disciplinary action(s), the same IncidentIdentifier should be used for all students. Each district/campus must develop a system for assigning incident numbers. The same incident numbers can be used on multiple campuses, since incident numbers must be unique at a campus, but not for the district.
IncidentIdentifier allows users to see the connection between two or more students involved in a single incident and/or two or more disciplinary actions for the same incident. The same IncidentIdentifier may appear on several DisciplineActions for a given student. The same IncidentIdentifier may also appear on the DisciplineActions of more than one student. A particular IncidentIdentifier may be duplicated for unrelated events across campuses in a particular district, but within a particular campus, the duplication of IncidentIdentifiers must be related to the same event.
IncidentDate is required in the Ed-Fi model and is mandatory for the entity to be loaded into the individual operational data store (IODS). IncidentDate will not be promoted to TSDS.
IncidentLocation (E1083) indicates where a student committed an applicable offense that is enumerated in TEC, §37.006 or §37.007 (On/off school property, school related activities, etc.).
The Behavior code identifies those Behaviors that have a location specified in the Texas Education Code Chapter 37. In most cases where the IncidentLocation applies to a particular Behavior, there is more than one possible action for that Behavior depending upon where the behavior occurred. If a Behavior only has an IncidentLocation of 00 (Not Applicable), then the Texas Education Code Chapter 37 is silent as to a location of the behavior and it does not matter where the behavior occurred so long as the local Student Code of Conduct addresses the LEA’s ability to take action for the behavior where it occurred.
Please refer to the PEIMS Discipline Data for guidance to all Behaviors, the related IncidentLocations, and the allowable actions per Texas Education Code Chapter 37.

=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
Special Requirements: ## SR1
LEA organization changes must be updated through the AskTED system before loading data into the Individual Operational Data Store (IODS). Updating the AskTED system will enable the TSDS system to accurately identify an LEA during the data submission process.
## SR2
Special Education Data System (SPEDS) - Summer Submission:
PreschoolOutcomesReporting (E3098) must be reported with “true” when no students are reported for SPP Indicator 7 Preschool Outcomes.
TimelyInitialEvaluationReporting (E3126) must be reported with “true” when no students are reported for SPP Indicator 11 Timely Initial Evaluation (Child Find).
EarlyChildhoodTransitionReporting (E3127) must be reported with “true” when no students are reported for SPP Indicator 12 Early Childhood Transition.
SecondaryTransitionReporting (E3128) must be reported with “true” when no students are reported for reporting SPP Indicator 13 Secondary Transition.
