elements.business_rules_text:
=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
For TSDS reporting, every Local Education Agency (LEA) must report the appropriate School entity data based on the collection and status of the campus in AskTED.
PEIMS Fall Enrollment Submission (6):
Report one School entity for each active instructional campus registered in AskTED.
PEIMS Fall Submission (1):
Report one School entity for each active instructional or under construction campus registered in AskTED.
PEIMS Midyear Submission (2):
Report one School entity for each campus registered in AskTED in the prior school year as active instructional or under construction.
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
Report one School entity for each active instructional campus registered in AskTED.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
Report one School entity for any campus reporting students in this collection. For example, students serviced through the Extended School Year (ESY) Services Program, Flexible Attendance Program, or Additional Days School Year Program (ADSY).
Core Collections:
Report one School entity for any campus reporting students in the collection. For example, report School if reporting students for SPPI-7, SPPI-11, SPPI-12, or SPPI-13.
An LEA cannot report the SchoolId number of another LEA in the School entity.
Texas Education Agency will pre-populate the LEAs Individual Operational Data Store (IODS) with the AskTED education organization data that is centrally managed by the Texas Education Agency (TEA). Additionally, TEA will pre-populate the LEAs IODS with the following administrative campuses: 000, 699, 701, 702, 703, 720, 750, 751, 998, and 999. When the data is promoted to the data mart, the LEA and campus names will be overwritten by the AskTED data.

Special Requirements: ## SR1
Campus organization changes must be updated through the AskTED system.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
EducationOrganizationCategory is required in the Ed-Fi model and is mandatory for the entity to be loaded into the Individual Operational Data Store (IODS). EducationOrganizationCategory will not be promoted to the TSDS.
NameOfInstitution (E3037) is the full, legally accepted name of the institution.
The NameOfInstitution is promoted to the data mart from AskTED.
LocalEducationAgency Reference
The LocalEducationAgency Reference represents the LEA of which the SchoolId is an organizational component registered with TEA.
SchoolId (E0266) indicates the unique campus identification number registered with the Texas Education Agency (TEA). It is the linking of LocalEducationAgencyId with the campus identification number.
An instructional campus:
- has an assigned administrator,
- has enrolled students who are counted for average daily attendance,
- has assigned instructional staff,
- receives federal, state, or local funds as its primary support,
- provides instruction in the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS),
- has one or more groups in the range from early education through grade 12, and
- is not a program for students enrolled in another public school.
An alternative instructional unit is an instructional site, center, program, or arrangement that is not governed by an individual campus organization, and does not meet the above standard definition of an instructional campus.
The campuses reported using the School entity must match a campus registered with the TEA for the current year.
A campus must not report a SchoolId with a number greater than 698 for the rightmost three digits.
The first six characters of the SchoolId must match the value of the LocalEducationAgencyId in the LEAs LocalEducationAgency entity.
GradeLevel (E0017) indicates the current grade level of the student, or the grade level(s) offered at a school.
PKFullDayWaiver (E1646) indicates whether the campus has received an exemption from offering a full-day prekindergarten program.
## DR2
AdditionalDaysProgram (E1671) indicates whether the campus implemented an Additional Days School Year (ADSY) program for any students in prekindergarten through eighth grades as described in TEC §48.0051.
The AdditionalDaysProgram is reported only for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) and PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4).
A campus offering an ADSY Program is only eligible for funding if they offer this program in addition to providing 175 instructional days and 75,600 instructional minutes during the regular school year for all attendance tracks.
The instruction for an ADSY program can be provided on a campus that is different from the campus in which a student is enrolled. The campus in which the student is enrolled during the current school year is required to meet the ADSY calendar requirements of 175 instructional days and 75,600 minutes.
For example, a Local Education Agency (LEA) has a centralized ADSY program for the summer. The campus in which the student was last enrolled must meet the calendar requirements and report the AdditionalDaysProgram (E1671).
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
The AdditionalDaysProgram is reported to indicate any campus that has students participating in the ADSY program. Between the first PEIMS Summer submission and resubmission, TEA will verify the reported calendar data to ensure the campus meets the minimum ADSY calendar requirements.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
Report all relevant ADSY program data.
## DR3
NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727) indicates the number of reported incidents of bullying at each campus as defined in TEC §37.0832.
A reported incident of bullying must meet the definition of bullying as defined in TEC §37.0832.
Bullying is defined as a single significant act or a pattern of acts by one or more students directed at another student that exploits an imbalance of power and involves engaging in written or verbal expression, expression through electronic means, or physical conduct that interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity, and:
- Has the effect or will have the effect of physically harming a student, damaging a student’s property, or placing a student in reasonable fear of harm to the student’s person or of damage to the student’s property;
- Is sufficiently severe, persistent, or pervasive enough that the action or threat creates an intimidating, threatening, or abusive educational environment for a student;
- Materially and substantially disrupts the educational process or the orderly operation of a classroom or school; or
- Infringes on the rights of the victim at school.
Bullying incidents include:
- Bullying that occurs on or is delivered to school property or to the site of a school-sponsored or school-related activity on or off school property,
- Bullying that occurs on a publicly or privately owned school bus or vehicle being used for transportation of students to or from school or a school-sponsored or school-related activity, and
- Cyberbullying that occurs off school property or outside of a school-sponsored or school-related activity if the cyberbullying interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity.
The NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727) is inclusive of the NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728). A reported incident of bullying may or may not result in a reportable disciplinary action.
NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728) indicates the number of reported incidents of cyberbullying at each campus as defined in TEC §37.0832.
Cyberbullying means bullying that is done through the use of any electronic communication device, including through the use of a cellular or other type of telephone, a computer, a camera, electronic mail, instant messaging, text messaging, a social media application, an Internet website, or any other Internet-based communication tool.
Cyberbullying incidents can occur:
- On or be delivered to school property or to the site of a school-sponsored or school-related activity on or off school property,
- On a publicly or privately owned school bus or vehicle being used for transportation of students to or from school or a school-sponsored or school-related activity, and
- Off school property or outside of a school-sponsored or school-related activity if the cyberbullying interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity.
The NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728) will be equal to or less than the NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727).
## DR4
ExpandedLearningOpportunity (E1613) indicates if a campus offers any expanded learning opportunity (ELO) as listed in TEC §33.252.
ExpandedLearningOpportunity is reported only for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) and PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4).
Additional guidance can be found below in the School>ELOSet.
School>CampusEnrollmentTypeSet
The CampusEnrollmentTypeSet captures the method by which the campus draws student enrollment and the BeginDate and EndDate associated with the CampusEnrollmentType data element.
CampusEnrollmentType (E1641) specifies the method by which the campus draws student enrollment.
This data element is reported in the PEIMS Fall Submission (1) and remains constant throughout the school year.
For additional guidance on determining CampusEnrollmentType, refer to the Campus Enrollment Type Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) at https://tea.texas.gov/perfreport/campus_enrollment_faq.aspx.
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day a campus is assigned to the CampusEnrollmentType descriptor.
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a campus was assigned to the CampusEnrollmentType descriptor.
## DR5
School>NSLPTypeSet
The NSLPTypeSet captures the campus’s participation status in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) and the BeginDate and EndDate associated with the NSLPType data element.
NSLPType (E1591) indicates a campus's National School Lunch Program (NSLP) participation status. The NSLP provides reimbursement to schools for free or reduced-price meals based on student eligibility.
Options for claiming reimbursement under the NSLP include eligibility determined:
- At the individual student/family level (participation in NSLP without using any Provision or the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP)) or
- At the campus/community level (Provision 2 or CEP).
The NSLPType is reported in PEIMS Fall Submission (1) only.
Following are the data sources to be used to document each descriptor located in the NSLPTypeDescriptor table:
- 01 - The Standard Accounting and Claiming option requires that participating schools distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application forms for each family enrolling students in the school.
- 02 - The Provision 2 option requires schools to distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application forms for each family enrolling students in the school only in the first year of operation.
- 03 - The CEP option describes a lunch program where schools do not distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application form for each family enrolling students in this school. Instead, schools participating in the CEP program use the direct certification list provided by the Texas Department of Agriculture (TDA).
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day in the current school year a campus is assigned to the NSLPType descriptor.
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a campus was assigned to the NSLPType descriptor.
## DR6
School>CharterWaitlistSet
The CharterWaitlistSet captures the data elements required to be reported by charter schools for the Charter School Waitlist Collection per TEC §§12.1173 and 12.1174. These data elements are only reported by charter schools for the Charter School Waitlist Collection.
NumberCharterStudentsEnrolled (E1674) indicates the number of students enrolled at a charter school campus as of the last Friday in September.
CharterEducationalEnrollmentCapacity (E1675) indicates the number of students to which the charter school campus is able to provide instruction without exceeding staffing and facility limitations and the approved charter holder's maximum enrollment.
CharterAdmissionWaitlist (E1676) indicates whether the charter school campus uses a waitlist for admission.
## DR7
School>ELOSet
The ELOSet captures data for school participation in an ELO.
ELOType (E1614) indicates the type of expanded learning opportunity (ELO) program offered at the campus.
If the school offers an ELO program, then the following elements must be provided for each ELO activity offered:
- ELOType (E1614)
- ELOActivity (E1719)
- ELODaysScheduledPerYear (E1720)
- ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay (E1621)
School>ELOSet>ELOActivitySet
The ELOActivitySet captures the specific ELO activities offered at a campus and the days and minutes scheduled per year of each ELO offering.
There can be more than one ELOActivitySet reported for an ELOType.
For example, if a school offers both a Non-Voluntary Extended School Year and a Voluntary Expanded Learning – Before School, report both sets of data in their own ELOType.
ELOActivity (E1719) indicates the specific Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) activity offered at the campus.
There are six ELO Activity codes that can be reported:
- 01 – Rigorous Coursework is defined as a TEKS-aligned and credit-earning course, including dual credit and credit recovery activities.
- 02 – Mentoring is defined as scheduled interaction between a trained adult and a specific student in which the adult provides support and life skills to help the student’s personal and academic development.
- 03 – Tutoring is defined as a one-on-one or small group, led by a certified teacher that provides content instruction or homework help. Tutoring does not include academic skill-building activities.
- 04 – Physical Activity is defined as activities designed to provide students with supplemental non-UIL opportunities for individual or group exercise, or related knowledge and skills that encourage regular physical activity.
- 05 – Academic Support is defined as supplemental support related to student academic skill development and may include compensatory education, test-taking skills, and related academic skill-building. Tutoring and homework help are not considered academic support.
- 06 – Educational Enrichment includes activities that engage students in actively exploring academic content and activities introduced during the regular school day. It consists of activities that are intentionally designed to align with but not replicate the instruction in a core course to increase the academic success of students in any subject, including fine arts, civic engagement, science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
ELODaysScheduledPerYear (E1720) is the number of days the Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) activity is offered during the school year.
ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay (E1621) indicates the number of minutes scheduled for an Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) each day.
The minimum amount of time a given ELOType can be provided under a given ELOActivity must be 45 consecutive minutes.
A campus offers Tutoring in both English and Math, and both are provided before school. The ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay will need to be added together and reported as one total since they are the same ELOActivity under the same ELOType.
Additionally, if a school offers the same ELO activity throughout the year, but changes the length of minutes scheduled per day, the minutes will need to be averaged for reporting purposes.
For example, a school offers Academic Support for 60 minutes on Mondays and 90 minutes on Wednesdays. The minutes will need to be averaged to 75 minutes/day for reporting purposes.

SchoolId (E0266) indicates the unique campus identification number registered with the Texas Education Agency (TEA). It is the linking of LocalEducationAgencyId with the campus identification number.
An instructional campus:
- has an assigned administrator,
- has enrolled students who are counted for average daily attendance,
- has assigned instructional staff,
- receives federal, state, or local funds as its primary support,
- provides instruction in the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS),
- has one or more groups in the range from early education through grade 12, and
- is not a program for students enrolled in another public school.
An alternative instructional unit is an instructional site, center, program, or arrangement that is not governed by an individual campus organization, and does not meet the above standard definition of an instructional campus.
The campuses reported using the School entity must match a campus registered with the TEA for the current year.
A campus must not report a SchoolId with a number greater than 698 for the rightmost three digits.
The first six characters of the SchoolId must match the value of the LocalEducationAgencyId in the LEAs LocalEducationAgency entity.
GradeLevel (E0017) indicates the current grade level of the student, or the grade level(s) offered at a school.
PKFullDayWaiver (E1646) indicates whether the campus has received an exemption from offering a full-day prekindergarten program.
## DR2
AdditionalDaysProgram (E1671) indicates whether the campus implemented an Additional Days School Year (ADSY) program for any students in prekindergarten through eighth grades as described in TEC §48.0051.
The AdditionalDaysProgram is reported only for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) and PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4).
A campus offering an ADSY Program is only eligible for funding if they offer this program in addition to providing 175 instructional days and 75,600 instructional minutes during the regular school year for all attendance tracks.
The instruction for an ADSY program can be provided on a campus that is different from the campus in which a student is enrolled. The campus in which the student is enrolled during the current school year is required to meet the ADSY calendar requirements of 175 instructional days and 75,600 minutes.
For example, a Local Education Agency (LEA) has a centralized ADSY program for the summer. The campus in which the student was last enrolled must meet the calendar requirements and report the AdditionalDaysProgram (E1671).
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
The AdditionalDaysProgram is reported to indicate any campus that has students participating in the ADSY program. Between the first PEIMS Summer submission and resubmission, TEA will verify the reported calendar data to ensure the campus meets the minimum ADSY calendar requirements.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
Report all relevant ADSY program data.
## DR3
NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727) indicates the number of reported incidents of bullying at each campus as defined in TEC §37.0832.
A reported incident of bullying must meet the definition of bullying as defined in TEC §37.0832.
Bullying is defined as a single significant act or a pattern of acts by one or more students directed at another student that exploits an imbalance of power and involves engaging in written or verbal expression, expression through electronic means, or physical conduct that interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity, and:
- Has the effect or will have the effect of physically harming a student, damaging a student’s property, or placing a student in reasonable fear of harm to the student’s person or of damage to the student’s property;
- Is sufficiently severe, persistent, or pervasive enough that the action or threat creates an intimidating, threatening, or abusive educational environment for a student;
- Materially and substantially disrupts the educational process or the orderly operation of a classroom or school; or
- Infringes on the rights of the victim at school.
Bullying incidents include:
- Bullying that occurs on or is delivered to school property or to the site of a school-sponsored or school-related activity on or off school property,
- Bullying that occurs on a publicly or privately owned school bus or vehicle being used for transportation of students to or from school or a school-sponsored or school-related activity, and
- Cyberbullying that occurs off school property or outside of a school-sponsored or school-related activity if the cyberbullying interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity.
The NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727) is inclusive of the NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728). A reported incident of bullying may or may not result in a reportable disciplinary action.
NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728) indicates the number of reported incidents of cyberbullying at each campus as defined in TEC §37.0832.
Cyberbullying means bullying that is done through the use of any electronic communication device, including through the use of a cellular or other type of telephone, a computer, a camera, electronic mail, instant messaging, text messaging, a social media application, an Internet website, or any other Internet-based communication tool.
Cyberbullying incidents can occur:
- On or be delivered to school property or to the site of a school-sponsored or school-related activity on or off school property,
- On a publicly or privately owned school bus or vehicle being used for transportation of students to or from school or a school-sponsored or school-related activity, and
- Off school property or outside of a school-sponsored or school-related activity if the cyberbullying interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity.
The NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728) will be equal to or less than the NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727).
## DR4
ExpandedLearningOpportunity (E1613) indicates if a campus offers any expanded learning opportunity (ELO) as listed in TEC §33.252.
ExpandedLearningOpportunity is reported only for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) and PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4).
Additional guidance can be found below in the School>ELOSet.
School>CampusEnrollmentTypeSet
The CampusEnrollmentTypeSet captures the method by which the campus draws student enrollment and the BeginDate and EndDate associated with the CampusEnrollmentType data element.
CampusEnrollmentType (E1641) specifies the method by which the campus draws student enrollment.
This data element is reported in the PEIMS Fall Submission (1) and remains constant throughout the school year.
For additional guidance on determining CampusEnrollmentType, refer to the Campus Enrollment Type Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) at https://tea.texas.gov/perfreport/campus_enrollment_faq.aspx.
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day a campus is assigned to the CampusEnrollmentType descriptor.
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a campus was assigned to the CampusEnrollmentType descriptor.
## DR5
School>NSLPTypeSet
The NSLPTypeSet captures the campus’s participation status in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) and the BeginDate and EndDate associated with the NSLPType data element.
NSLPType (E1591) indicates a campus's National School Lunch Program (NSLP) participation status. The NSLP provides reimbursement to schools for free or reduced-price meals based on student eligibility.
Options for claiming reimbursement under the NSLP include eligibility determined:
- At the individual student/family level (participation in NSLP without using any Provision or the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP)) or
- At the campus/community level (Provision 2 or CEP).
The NSLPType is reported in PEIMS Fall Submission (1) only.
Following are the data sources to be used to document each descriptor located in the NSLPTypeDescriptor table:
- 01 - The Standard Accounting and Claiming option requires that participating schools distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application forms for each family enrolling students in the school.
- 02 - The Provision 2 option requires schools to distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application forms for each family enrolling students in the school only in the first year of operation.
- 03 - The CEP option describes a lunch program where schools do not distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application form for each family enrolling students in this school. Instead, schools participating in the CEP program use the direct certification list provided by the Texas Department of Agriculture (TDA).
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day in the current school year a campus is assigned to the NSLPType descriptor.
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a campus was assigned to the NSLPType descriptor.
## DR6
School>CharterWaitlistSet
The CharterWaitlistSet captures the data elements required to be reported by charter schools for the Charter School Waitlist Collection per TEC §§12.1173 and 12.1174. These data elements are only reported by charter schools for the Charter School Waitlist Collection.
NumberCharterStudentsEnrolled (E1674) indicates the number of students enrolled at a charter school campus as of the last Friday in September.
CharterEducationalEnrollmentCapacity (E1675) indicates the number of students to which the charter school campus is able to provide instruction without exceeding staffing and facility limitations and the approved charter holder's maximum enrollment.
CharterAdmissionWaitlist (E1676) indicates whether the charter school campus uses a waitlist for admission.
## DR7
School>ELOSet
The ELOSet captures data for school participation in an ELO.
ELOType (E1614) indicates the type of expanded learning opportunity (ELO) program offered at the campus.
If the school offers an ELO program, then the following elements must be provided for each ELO activity offered:
- ELOType (E1614)
- ELOActivity (E1719)
- ELODaysScheduledPerYear (E1720)
- ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay (E1621)

The ELOActivitySet captures the specific ELO activities offered at a campus and the days and minutes scheduled per year of each ELO offering.
There can be more than one ELOActivitySet reported for an ELOType.
For example, if a school offers both a Non-Voluntary Extended School Year and a Voluntary Expanded Learning – Before School, report both sets of data in their own ELOType.
ELOActivity (E1719) indicates the specific Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) activity offered at the campus.
There are six ELO Activity codes that can be reported:
- 01 – Rigorous Coursework is defined as a TEKS-aligned and credit-earning course, including dual credit and credit recovery activities.
- 02 – Mentoring is defined as scheduled interaction between a trained adult and a specific student in which the adult provides support and life skills to help the student’s personal and academic development.
- 03 – Tutoring is defined as a one-on-one or small group, led by a certified teacher that provides content instruction or homework help. Tutoring does not include academic skill-building activities.
- 04 – Physical Activity is defined as activities designed to provide students with supplemental non-UIL opportunities for individual or group exercise, or related knowledge and skills that encourage regular physical activity.
- 05 – Academic Support is defined as supplemental support related to student academic skill development and may include compensatory education, test-taking skills, and related academic skill-building. Tutoring and homework help are not considered academic support.
- 06 – Educational Enrichment includes activities that engage students in actively exploring academic content and activities introduced during the regular school day. It consists of activities that are intentionally designed to align with but not replicate the instruction in a core course to increase the academic success of students in any subject, including fine arts, civic engagement, science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
ELODaysScheduledPerYear (E1720) is the number of days the Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) activity is offered during the school year.
ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay (E1621) indicates the number of minutes scheduled for an Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) each day.
The minimum amount of time a given ELOType can be provided under a given ELOActivity must be 45 consecutive minutes.
A campus offers Tutoring in both English and Math, and both are provided before school. The ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay will need to be added together and reported as one total since they are the same ELOActivity under the same ELOType.
Additionally, if a school offers the same ELO activity throughout the year, but changes the length of minutes scheduled per day, the minutes will need to be averaged for reporting purposes.
For example, a school offers Academic Support for 60 minutes on Mondays and 90 minutes on Wednesdays. The minutes will need to be averaged to 75 minutes/day for reporting purposes.

The campuses reported using the School entity must match a campus registered with the TEA for the current year.
A campus must not report a SchoolId with a number greater than 698 for the rightmost three digits.
The first six characters of the SchoolId must match the value of the LocalEducationAgencyId in the LEAs LocalEducationAgency entity.
GradeLevel (E0017) indicates the current grade level of the student, or the grade level(s) offered at a school.
PKFullDayWaiver (E1646) indicates whether the campus has received an exemption from offering a full-day prekindergarten program.
## DR2
AdditionalDaysProgram (E1671) indicates whether the campus implemented an Additional Days School Year (ADSY) program for any students in prekindergarten through eighth grades as described in TEC §48.0051.
The AdditionalDaysProgram is reported only for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) and PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4).
A campus offering an ADSY Program is only eligible for funding if they offer this program in addition to providing 175 instructional days and 75,600 instructional minutes during the regular school year for all attendance tracks.
The instruction for an ADSY program can be provided on a campus that is different from the campus in which a student is enrolled. The campus in which the student is enrolled during the current school year is required to meet the ADSY calendar requirements of 175 instructional days and 75,600 minutes.
For example, a Local Education Agency (LEA) has a centralized ADSY program for the summer. The campus in which the student was last enrolled must meet the calendar requirements and report the AdditionalDaysProgram (E1671).
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
The AdditionalDaysProgram is reported to indicate any campus that has students participating in the ADSY program. Between the first PEIMS Summer submission and resubmission, TEA will verify the reported calendar data to ensure the campus meets the minimum ADSY calendar requirements.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
Report all relevant ADSY program data.
## DR3
NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727) indicates the number of reported incidents of bullying at each campus as defined in TEC §37.0832.
A reported incident of bullying must meet the definition of bullying as defined in TEC §37.0832.
Bullying is defined as a single significant act or a pattern of acts by one or more students directed at another student that exploits an imbalance of power and involves engaging in written or verbal expression, expression through electronic means, or physical conduct that interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity, and:
- Has the effect or will have the effect of physically harming a student, damaging a student’s property, or placing a student in reasonable fear of harm to the student’s person or of damage to the student’s property;
- Is sufficiently severe, persistent, or pervasive enough that the action or threat creates an intimidating, threatening, or abusive educational environment for a student;
- Materially and substantially disrupts the educational process or the orderly operation of a classroom or school; or
- Infringes on the rights of the victim at school.

- Bullying that occurs on or is delivered to school property or to the site of a school-sponsored or school-related activity on or off school property,
- Bullying that occurs on a publicly or privately owned school bus or vehicle being used for transportation of students to or from school or a school-sponsored or school-related activity, and

NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728) indicates the number of reported incidents of cyberbullying at each campus as defined in TEC §37.0832.
Cyberbullying means bullying that is done through the use of any electronic communication device, including through the use of a cellular or other type of telephone, a computer, a camera, electronic mail, instant messaging, text messaging, a social media application, an Internet website, or any other Internet-based communication tool.
Cyberbullying incidents can occur:
- On or be delivered to school property or to the site of a school-sponsored or school-related activity on or off school property,
- On a publicly or privately owned school bus or vehicle being used for transportation of students to or from school or a school-sponsored or school-related activity, and
- Off school property or outside of a school-sponsored or school-related activity if the cyberbullying interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity.

The CampusEnrollmentTypeSet captures the method by which the campus draws student enrollment and the BeginDate and EndDate associated with the CampusEnrollmentType data element.

EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a campus was assigned to the CampusEnrollmentType descriptor.
## DR5
School>NSLPTypeSet
The NSLPTypeSet captures the campus’s participation status in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) and the BeginDate and EndDate associated with the NSLPType data element.
NSLPType (E1591) indicates a campus's National School Lunch Program (NSLP) participation status. The NSLP provides reimbursement to schools for free or reduced-price meals based on student eligibility.
Options for claiming reimbursement under the NSLP include eligibility determined:
- At the individual student/family level (participation in NSLP without using any Provision or the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP)) or
- At the campus/community level (Provision 2 or CEP).
The NSLPType is reported in PEIMS Fall Submission (1) only.
Following are the data sources to be used to document each descriptor located in the NSLPTypeDescriptor table:
- 01 - The Standard Accounting and Claiming option requires that participating schools distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application forms for each family enrolling students in the school.
- 02 - The Provision 2 option requires schools to distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application forms for each family enrolling students in the school only in the first year of operation.
- 03 - The CEP option describes a lunch program where schools do not distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application form for each family enrolling students in this school. Instead, schools participating in the CEP program use the direct certification list provided by the Texas Department of Agriculture (TDA).
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day in the current school year a campus is assigned to the NSLPType descriptor.
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a campus was assigned to the NSLPType descriptor.

## DR7
School>ELOSet
The ELOSet captures data for school participation in an ELO.

If the school offers an ELO program, then the following elements must be provided for each ELO activity offered:
- ELOType (E1614)
- ELOActivity (E1719)
- ELODaysScheduledPerYear (E1720)
- ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay (E1621)

- 01 – Rigorous Coursework is defined as a TEKS-aligned and credit-earning course, including dual credit and credit recovery activities.
- 02 – Mentoring is defined as scheduled interaction between a trained adult and a specific student in which the adult provides support and life skills to help the student’s personal and academic development.
- 03 – Tutoring is defined as a one-on-one or small group, led by a certified teacher that provides content instruction or homework help. Tutoring does not include academic skill-building activities.
- 04 – Physical Activity is defined as activities designed to provide students with supplemental non-UIL opportunities for individual or group exercise, or related knowledge and skills that encourage regular physical activity.
- 05 – Academic Support is defined as supplemental support related to student academic skill development and may include compensatory education, test-taking skills, and related academic skill-building. Tutoring and homework help are not considered academic support.
- 06 – Educational Enrichment includes activities that engage students in actively exploring academic content and activities introduced during the regular school day. ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay (E1621) indicates the number of minutes scheduled for an Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) each day.

For example, a school offers Academic Support for 60 minutes on Mondays and 90 minutes on Wednesdays. The minutes will need to be averaged to 75 minutes/day for reporting purposes.

## DR2
AdditionalDaysProgram (E1671) indicates whether the campus implemented an Additional Days School Year (ADSY) program for any students in prekindergarten through eighth grades as described in TEC §48.0051.
The AdditionalDaysProgram is reported only for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) and PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4).
A campus offering an ADSY Program is only eligible for funding if they offer this program in addition to providing 175 instructional days and 75,600 instructional minutes during the regular school year for all attendance tracks.
The instruction for an ADSY program can be provided on a campus that is different from the campus in which a student is enrolled. The campus in which the student is enrolled during the current school year is required to meet the ADSY calendar requirements of 175 instructional days and 75,600 minutes.
For example, a Local Education Agency (LEA) has a centralized ADSY program for the summer. The campus in which the student was last enrolled must meet the calendar requirements and report the AdditionalDaysProgram (E1671).
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
The AdditionalDaysProgram is reported to indicate any campus that has students participating in the ADSY program. Between the first PEIMS Summer submission and resubmission, TEA will verify the reported calendar data to ensure the campus meets the minimum ADSY calendar requirements.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
Report all relevant ADSY program data.
## DR3
NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727) indicates the number of reported incidents of bullying at each campus as defined in TEC §37.0832.
A reported incident of bullying must meet the definition of bullying as defined in TEC §37.0832.
Bullying is defined as a single significant act or a pattern of acts by one or more students directed at another student that exploits an imbalance of power and involves engaging in written or verbal expression, expression through electronic means, or physical conduct that interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity, and:
- Has the effect or will have the effect of physically harming a student, damaging a student’s property, or placing a student in reasonable fear of harm to the student’s person or of damage to the student’s property;
- Is sufficiently severe, persistent, or pervasive enough that the action or threat creates an intimidating, threatening, or abusive educational environment for a student;
- Materially and substantially disrupts the educational process or the orderly operation of a classroom or school; or
- Infringes on the rights of the victim at school.
Bullying incidents include:
- Bullying that occurs on or is delivered to school property or to the site of a school-sponsored or school-related activity on or off school property,
- Bullying that occurs on a publicly or privately owned school bus or vehicle being used for transportation of students to or from school or a school-sponsored or school-related activity, and
- Cyberbullying that occurs off school property or outside of a school-sponsored or school-related activity if the cyberbullying interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity.
The NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727) is inclusive of the NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728). A reported incident of bullying may or may not result in a reportable disciplinary action.
NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728) indicates the number of reported incidents of cyberbullying at each campus as defined in TEC §37.0832.
Cyberbullying means bullying that is done through the use of any electronic communication device, including through the use of a cellular or other type of telephone, a computer, a camera, electronic mail, instant messaging, text messaging, a social media application, an Internet website, or any other Internet-based communication tool.
Cyberbullying incidents can occur:
- On or be delivered to school property or to the site of a school-sponsored or school-related activity on or off school property,
- On a publicly or privately owned school bus or vehicle being used for transportation of students to or from school or a school-sponsored or school-related activity, and
- Off school property or outside of a school-sponsored or school-related activity if the cyberbullying interferes with a student’s educational opportunities or substantially disrupts the orderly operation of a classroom, school, or school-sponsored or school-related activity.
The NumberOfCyberbullyingIncidents (E1728) will be equal to or less than the NumberOfBullyingIncidents (E1727).
## DR4
ExpandedLearningOpportunity (E1613) indicates if a campus offers any expanded learning opportunity (ELO) as listed in TEC §33.252.
ExpandedLearningOpportunity is reported only for PEIMS Summer Submission (3) and PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4).
Additional guidance can be found below in the School>ELOSet.
School>CampusEnrollmentTypeSet
The CampusEnrollmentTypeSet captures the method by which the campus draws student enrollment and the BeginDate and EndDate associated with the CampusEnrollmentType data element.
CampusEnrollmentType (E1641) specifies the method by which the campus draws student enrollment.
This data element is reported in the PEIMS Fall Submission (1) and remains constant throughout the school year.
For additional guidance on determining CampusEnrollmentType, refer to the Campus Enrollment Type Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) at https://tea.texas.gov/perfreport/campus_enrollment_faq.aspx.
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day a campus is assigned to the CampusEnrollmentType descriptor.
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a campus was assigned to the CampusEnrollmentType descriptor.
## DR5
School>NSLPTypeSet
The NSLPTypeSet captures the campus’s participation status in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) and the BeginDate and EndDate associated with the NSLPType data element.
NSLPType (E1591) indicates a campus's National School Lunch Program (NSLP) participation status. The NSLP provides reimbursement to schools for free or reduced-price meals based on student eligibility.
Options for claiming reimbursement under the NSLP include eligibility determined:
- At the individual student/family level (participation in NSLP without using any Provision or the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP)) or
- At the campus/community level (Provision 2 or CEP).
The NSLPType is reported in PEIMS Fall Submission (1) only.
Following are the data sources to be used to document each descriptor located in the NSLPTypeDescriptor table:
- 01 - The Standard Accounting and Claiming option requires that participating schools distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application forms for each family enrolling students in the school.
- 02 - The Provision 2 option requires schools to distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application forms for each family enrolling students in the school only in the first year of operation.
- 03 - The CEP option describes a lunch program where schools do not distribute and retrieve the official NSLP application form for each family enrolling students in this school. Instead, schools participating in the CEP program use the direct certification list provided by the Texas Department of Agriculture (TDA).
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day in the current school year a campus is assigned to the NSLPType descriptor.
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a campus was assigned to the NSLPType descriptor.
## DR6
School>CharterWaitlistSet
The CharterWaitlistSet captures the data elements required to be reported by charter schools for the Charter School Waitlist Collection per TEC §§12.1173 and 12.1174. These data elements are only reported by charter schools for the Charter School Waitlist Collection.
NumberCharterStudentsEnrolled (E1674) indicates the number of students enrolled at a charter school campus as of the last Friday in September.
CharterEducationalEnrollmentCapacity (E1675) indicates the number of students to which the charter school campus is able to provide instruction without exceeding staffing and facility limitations and the approved charter holder's maximum enrollment.
CharterAdmissionWaitlist (E1676) indicates whether the charter school campus uses a waitlist for admission.
## DR7
School>ELOSet
The ELOSet captures data for school participation in an ELO.
ELOType (E1614) indicates the type of expanded learning opportunity (ELO) program offered at the campus.
If the school offers an ELO program, then the following elements must be provided for each ELO activity offered:
- ELOType (E1614)
- ELOActivity (E1719)
- ELODaysScheduledPerYear (E1720)
- ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay (E1621)
School>ELOSet>ELOActivitySet
The ELOActivitySet captures the specific ELO activities offered at a campus and the days and minutes scheduled per year of each ELO offering.
There can be more than one ELOActivitySet reported for an ELOType.
For example, if a school offers both a Non-Voluntary Extended School Year and a Voluntary Expanded Learning – Before School, report both sets of data in their own ELOType.
ELOActivity (E1719) indicates the specific Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) activity offered at the campus.
There are six ELO Activity codes that can be reported:
- 01 – Rigorous Coursework is defined as a TEKS-aligned and credit-earning course, including dual credit and credit recovery activities.
- 02 – Mentoring is defined as scheduled interaction between a trained adult and a specific student in which the adult provides support and life skills to help the student’s personal and academic development.
- 03 – Tutoring is defined as a one-on-one or small group, led by a certified teacher that provides content instruction or homework help. Tutoring does not include academic skill-building activities.
- 04 – Physical Activity is defined as activities designed to provide students with supplemental non-UIL opportunities for individual or group exercise, or related knowledge and skills that encourage regular physical activity.
- 05 – Academic Support is defined as supplemental support related to student academic skill development and may include compensatory education, test-taking skills, and related academic skill-building. Tutoring and homework help are not considered academic support.
- 06 – Educational Enrichment includes activities that engage students in actively exploring academic content and activities introduced during the regular school day. It consists of activities that are intentionally designed to align with but not replicate the instruction in a core course to increase the academic success of students in any subject, including fine arts, civic engagement, science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
ELODaysScheduledPerYear (E1720) is the number of days the Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) activity is offered during the school year.
ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay (E1621) indicates the number of minutes scheduled for an Expanded Learning Opportunity (ELO) each day.
The minimum amount of time a given ELOType can be provided under a given ELOActivity must be 45 consecutive minutes.
A campus offers Tutoring in both English and Math, and both are provided before school. The ELOMinutesScheduledPerDay will need to be added together and reported as one total since they are the same ELOActivity under the same ELOType.
Additionally, if a school offers the same ELO activity throughout the year, but changes the length of minutes scheduled per day, the minutes will need to be averaged for reporting purposes.
For example, a school offers Academic Support for 60 minutes on Mondays and 90 minutes on Wednesdays. The minutes will need to be averaged to 75 minutes/day for reporting purposes.

elements.business_rules_text:
=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
Information from the Section Entity is used to capture the complete course offerings for a particular campus. This information is then used with the data submitted for staff and student course participation to identify the classes enrolled in by students and taught by teachers.
## GR2
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
A Section Entity is reported for sections in the current school year for:
- each unique high school credit course
A Section Entity should be reported for all high school credit courses offered through a campus regardless of the method of instruction delivery.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
A Section Entity is reported for sections during the summer (between school years) for:
- high school Career and Technical Education (CTE) course,
- dual credit course,
- College Preparatory Course English Language Arts, or
- College Preparatory Course Mathematics.
A Section Entity should be reported for all courses offered through a campus regardless of the method of instruction delivery.
## GR3
Class Roster Winter Submission:
A Section Entity is reported for all courses offered in grade levels EE-12 as of the last Friday in February. Each Section Entity should have at least one corresponding StaffSectionAssociation Entity for the teacher and a corresponding StudentSectionAssociation Entity for each student assigned to that course. CourseCodes that begin with "SA," "SE," "SR," "SS," or "8" are not promoted.
A Section Entity reported with a NonCampusBasedInstruction (C182) 00 (Not Applicable) must be reported with at least one StaffSectionAssociation.
Early Childhood Data System (ECDS) Collections:
For the ECDS collection, each campus that enrolls and serves prekindergarten and kindergarten students must report at least one Section Entity for every prekindergarten or kindergarten course taught. No Section Entities are reported for grade level EE.

Special Requirements: ## SR1
For students that are placed in or are expelled to a Disciplinary Alternative Education Program (DAEP), or expelled to a Juvenile Justice Alternative Education Program (JJAEP), the campus that enrolls the student during these disciplinary removals is responsible for creating a Section Entity that reflect the new course sections to which the student has been assigned while attending a DAEP or a JJAEP.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
CourseOffering Reference
The CourseOffering Reference represents the identifier assigned to the CourseOffering.
SectionIdentifier (E1056) is a number identifying a unique course section that is unique for a particular school year, campus, and Course.
The SectionIdentifier must be unique such that multiple teachers can be linked to a single course section through the StaffSectionAssociation and students enrolled in a unique course section can be identified by the SectionIdentifier on the Section Entity.
The SectionIdentifier may be any 255 character district defined identifier comprised of letters and numbers.
## DR2
Section>SectionSet
PopulationServed (E0747) identifies the student population for which a section has been designed or is intended. It does not necessarily identify the program eligibility of the students who receive the service.
The correct descriptor is determined by the population for which the service was designed, not the student population that receives a service. If two or more populations are being served, only one record should be reported, using the population for which the service was designed. If intent cannot be determined, use descriptor 01 (regular students).
## DR3
SPEDStudentAgeRange (E3059) identifies the age range of students receiving special education services that teaching and paraprofessional staff provided services to.
A SPEDStudentAgeRange other than 00 (Not Providing Special Education Services to Students) is only reported for a Section designed for PopulationServed 06 (Students Receiving Special Education Services). If students receiving special education services are from more than one age range are taking the course, more than one Section entity may need to be reported.
SPEDStudentAgeRange
Descriptor


Short Description


 






00


Not Providing Services to Students Receiving Special Education Services


The section is not designed for PopulationServed 06 (Students Receiving Special Education Services).




01


Providing Services to Students Aged 3 through 5 (not in Kindergarten)


The section is designed for PopulationServed 06 (Students Receiving Special Education Services) aged three through five. Students aged five are not yet enrolled in Kindergarten.




02


Providing Services to Students Aged 5 (in Kindergarten) through Age 21


The section is designed for PopulationServed 06 (Students Receiving Special Education Services) aged five in kindergarten through age 21.
CourseSequence (E0948) identifies the unique part(s) of a course when a course is taught during a single grading period or semester or across multiple grading periods or semesters.
The CourseSequence identifies how the course was taught to the student during the school year, or in the summer.  The CourseSequence identifies the order in which the course was scheduled in the class scheduling system. CourseSequence 1 (First Half Of A Two Semester Course) or D1 (First Half of a Two Semester Dual Credit Course) must be used for the first semester of a two-semester course, no matter if the course is taken in the fall or spring semester.
Dual credit CourseSequences are used for dual credit courses only. The length of the course for dual credit courses refers to the length of the college course, not the high school course.
## DR4
NonCampusBasedInstruction (E1072) indicates that a course was offered for class credit or student achievement, but 1) was not taught by a school district/charter school employee or a contracted teacher, or 2) was taught by a school district/charter school employee or a contracted teacher at a facility other than the campus where the student is enrolled.
Examples include but are not limited to college-based instruction, non-district teacher, non-campus teacher, internet-based instruction, and Texas Virtual School Network (TxVSN).
NonCampusBasedInstruction
Descriptor


Short Description


 






01


College Campus Based Course


College course (usually a dual credit course) taught either on a college campus or a high school campus by an instructor not employed by the LEA. College courses taught on a high school campus by an LEA teacher with college credentials cannot be reported with NonCampusBasedInstruction 01 (College Campus Based Course).




02


Electronic/Internet/Correspondence Based/Video Conferencing Course


Any course that is taught not using an actual teacher (Classroom Position 01 (Teacher of Record), 02 (Assistant Teacher), 03 (Support Teacher), or 04 (Substitute Teacher)) in the classroom where the student(s) meet for the class. Examples include, but are not limited to, internet delivered curriculum, academic instructional software programs, video instruction (live or recorded), online courses, etc.




03


Non-District Teacher Providing Classroom Instruction Services


A course taught by a teacher that is employed by another LEA. The “classroom” could be at any suitable location. Do not use this for reporting college instructors.




04


Texas Virtual School Network (TxVSN) Online Schools program


This is a full-time virtual program available only to eligible students in grade levels 3 - 12 who are enrolled in an eligible LEA participating in the program. For additional information and rules refer to the Student Attendance Accounting Handbook. In order for a school to receive state funding for students enrolled in the TxVSN online school, all TxVSN Online Schools program course sections offered to students must be reported using this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor. (Valid through the 2026-2027 School Year)




05


Texas Virtual School Network (TxVSN) Statewide Online Course Catalog


This program provides a supplemental statewide online course catalog of high school, advanced placement, and dual credit courses to eligible students in grade levels 9 - 12 who are enrolled in the LEA. For additional information refer to the Student Attendance Accounting Handbook. In order for a school to receive state funding for students enrolled in courses offered through the TxVSN statewide course catalog, all TxVSN Statewide course catalog course sections offered to students must be reported using this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor. (Valid through the 2026-2027 School Year)




06


Non-Campus Teacher Providing Instruction at Another District Facility


These courses are taught in the district at a location that does not have its own campus number. An example of this would be when the CTE program courses are all taught at a central CTE location that is not eligible for its own campus number. These teachers are not associated with any other campus in the LEA.




07


Juvenile Justice Alternative Education Program (JJAEP) - TEC §37.011


These courses are always taught at a JJAEP that has been established in accordance with TEC 37.011 and are taught by teachers that are hired or are paid for by the JJAEP.




08


Credit by Exam


This NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor reflects those courses for which a student earned credit through the official credit by exam process.




09


Out of District DAEP Program


This NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor reflects those courses that a student is assigned to while placed in a DAEP that is physically located in another LEA. While this is similar to 03 (Non-District Teacher Providing Classroom Instruction Services), it is limited to those instances of a student attending a DAEP that is physically under the control of another school district or charter school.




10


Non-District PE Substitution Program


The use of this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor is limited to those cases where the LEA has authorized a student to earn PE credit by participating in a physical education activity that is not offered by the LEA. These include such things as gymnastic organizations, etc.




11


Optional Flexible School Day Online Dropout Recovery Program – TEC §29.081 (e-2)


The use of this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor is when a dropout recovery program is offered through an internet based online program. Among other provisions, online dropout recovery education programs are specifically required to:

include as part of its curriculum credentials, certifications, and other course offerings that relates directly to employment in the state;
provide an academic coach or local advocate for each student;
use an individual learning plan to monitor each student's progress, and
track the number of minutes the student is receiving instruction online.





12


Local Virtual Course


Any course where instruction and content are delivered synchronously or asynchronously primarily over the Internet. (TEC §30B.001(7))




13


Statewide Virtual Course


Virtual courses offered by school systems in the state to any student regardless of where the student is enrolled.




99


Other


The use of this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor is limited to those situations where no other NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor listed above applies.
 
For example, the teacher, if applicable, in the classroom is not employed by or under direct contract to the LEA. 
 
The use of this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor should be rare.
## DR5
ClassType (E1055) identifies the type of class providing instruction to students in particular class settings.
ClassType is used to differentiate classes providing instruction in a regular setting classroom from non-regular classrooms. Class size is computed on regular classes.
ClassType
Descriptor


Short Description


 






01


Regular


All settings not mentioned below including regular classroom, laboratory, or shop settings




02


Non-regular


All other settings (including but not limited to):

In-School Suspension
School-Community Guidance Center
Disciplinary Alternative Education School Program
Televised Instruction
Non-disciplinary Alternative Education
Special Education
Residential Care and Treatment Facility
CTEHours (E3011) indicate the number of contact hours assigned to a particular section of a course.
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day in the current school year the data elements in the SectionSet are associated to the section.
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day in the current school year the data elements in the SectionSet were associated to the section.
## DR6
The following data elements are reported as part of the ECDS PK submission and only reported for the PK CourseCode (01010000, 01020100).
PKCurricula (E1579) indicates curricula used in the district’s prekindergarten program serving eligible four-year-old students per TEC 29.1532(c)(7).
HighQualityPKProgram (E1580) Indicates campus/course/section participation in the High-Quality Prekindergarten Program consistent with requirements in TEC §29.167-29.171.
High-quality prekindergarten components are mandatory for classrooms serving eligible four-year-olds. This indicator should not be marked for classrooms serving only PK3 students.
PKStudentInstruction (E1558) indicates the prekindergarten student type of instruction.
PKSchoolType (E1555) indicates the type of prekindergarten program that is offered.
PKSchoolType
Descriptor


Short Description


 






01


Non-Public Pre-K Head Start


Standalone Head Start not associated with a school district.




02


Public Pre-K


Public-school program implementing a prekindergarten program (excluding partnerships).




05


Non-Public Pre-K Licensed Child Care


Standalone childcare provider not associated with a school district.




07


Public Pre-K Head Start (LEA Grantee)


Public prekindergarten program where the LEA is the Head Start grantee. (This PKSchoolType descriptor will NOT require the LEA to submit a ChildCareOperationNumber (E1726).)




08


Public Pre-K Licensed Child Care


Public prekindergarten program that partner directly with a licensed childcare provider to dually enroll students (includes partnership classrooms where children are dually enrolled in both the LEA and childcare provider site). (This PKSchoolType descriptor WILL require the LEA to submit a ChildCareOperationNumber (E1726).)




10


Non-Public Pre-K


Private prekindergarten provider not associated with a school district.




11


In-District Charter Partnership


Prekindergarten program that is operated through an in-district charter partnership. The board of the LEA has authorized a non-profit organization, government entity, institute of higher education, or an existing charter as an in-district charter. (This PKSchoolType descriptor WILL require the LEA to submit a ChildCareOperationNumber (E1726), if partnering with a licensed provider. If the partnering provider is NOT licensed, eight zeros, "00000000", must be entered.)




12


Public Pre-K Head Start (Non-LEA Grantee)


Public prekindergarten programs that partner with a Head Start program and the Head Start grantee is not an LEA. (This PKSchoolType descriptor WILL require the LEA to submit a ChildCareOperationNumber (E1726), if partnering with a licensed provider. If the partnering provider is NOT licensed, eight zeros, "00000000", must be entered.)




99


Other


None of the descriptors above describe the LEA implemented program.

elements.business_rules_text:
=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
Information from the Section Entity is used to capture the complete course offerings for a particular campus. This information is then used with the data submitted for staff and student course participation to identify the classes enrolled in by students and taught by teachers.
## GR2
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
A Section Entity is reported for sections in the current school year for:
- each unique high school credit course
A Section Entity should be reported for all high school credit courses offered through a campus regardless of the method of instruction delivery.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
A Section Entity is reported for sections during the summer (between school years) for:
- high school Career and Technical Education (CTE) course,
- dual credit course,
- College Preparatory Course English Language Arts, or
- College Preparatory Course Mathematics.
A Section Entity should be reported for all courses offered through a campus regardless of the method of instruction delivery.
## GR3
Class Roster Winter Submission:
A Section Entity is reported for all courses offered in grade levels EE-12 as of the last Friday in February. Each Section Entity should have at least one corresponding StaffSectionAssociation Entity for the teacher and a corresponding StudentSectionAssociation Entity for each student assigned to that course. CourseCodes that begin with "SA," "SE," "SR," "SS," or "8" are not promoted.
A Section Entity reported with a NonCampusBasedInstruction (C182) 00 (Not Applicable) must be reported with at least one StaffSectionAssociation.
Early Childhood Data System (ECDS) Collections:
For the ECDS collection, each campus that enrolls and serves prekindergarten and kindergarten students must report at least one Section Entity for every prekindergarten or kindergarten course taught. No Section Entities are reported for grade level EE.

Special Requirements: ## SR1
For students that are placed in or are expelled to a Disciplinary Alternative Education Program (DAEP), or expelled to a Juvenile Justice Alternative Education Program (JJAEP), the campus that enrolls the student during these disciplinary removals is responsible for creating a Section Entity that reflect the new course sections to which the student has been assigned while attending a DAEP or a JJAEP.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
CourseOffering Reference
The CourseOffering Reference represents the identifier assigned to the CourseOffering.
SectionIdentifier (E1056) is a number identifying a unique course section that is unique for a particular school year, campus, and Course.
The SectionIdentifier must be unique such that multiple teachers can be linked to a single course section through the StaffSectionAssociation and students enrolled in a unique course section can be identified by the SectionIdentifier on the Section Entity.
The SectionIdentifier may be any 255 character district defined identifier comprised of letters and numbers.
## DR2
Section>SectionSet
PopulationServed (E0747) identifies the student population for which a section has been designed or is intended. It does not necessarily identify the program eligibility of the students who receive the service.
The correct descriptor is determined by the population for which the service was designed, not the student population that receives a service. If two or more populations are being served, only one record should be reported, using the population for which the service was designed. If intent cannot be determined, use descriptor 01 (regular students).
## DR3
SPEDStudentAgeRange (E3059) identifies the age range of students receiving special education services that teaching and paraprofessional staff provided services to.
A SPEDStudentAgeRange other than 00 (Not Providing Special Education Services to Students) is only reported for a Section designed for PopulationServed 06 (Students Receiving Special Education Services). If students receiving special education services are from more than one age range are taking the course, more than one Section entity may need to be reported.
SPEDStudentAgeRange
Descriptor


Short Description


 






00


Not Providing Services to Students Receiving Special Education Services


The section is not designed for PopulationServed 06 (Students Receiving Special Education Services).




01


Providing Services to Students Aged 3 through 5 (not in Kindergarten)


The section is designed for PopulationServed 06 (Students Receiving Special Education Services) aged three through five. Students aged five are not yet enrolled in Kindergarten.




02


Providing Services to Students Aged 5 (in Kindergarten) through Age 21


The section is designed for PopulationServed 06 (Students Receiving Special Education Services) aged five in kindergarten through age 21.
CourseSequence (E0948) identifies the unique part(s) of a course when a course is taught during a single grading period or semester or across multiple grading periods or semesters.
The CourseSequence identifies how the course was taught to the student during the school year, or in the summer.  The CourseSequence identifies the order in which the course was scheduled in the class scheduling system. CourseSequence 1 (First Half Of A Two Semester Course) or D1 (First Half of a Two Semester Dual Credit Course) must be used for the first semester of a two-semester course, no matter if the course is taken in the fall or spring semester.
Dual credit CourseSequences are used for dual credit courses only. The length of the course for dual credit courses refers to the length of the college course, not the high school course.
## DR4
NonCampusBasedInstruction (E1072) indicates that a course was offered for class credit or student achievement, but 1) was not taught by a school district/charter school employee or a contracted teacher, or 2) was taught by a school district/charter school employee or a contracted teacher at a facility other than the campus where the student is enrolled.
Examples include but are not limited to college-based instruction, non-district teacher, non-campus teacher, internet-based instruction, and Texas Virtual School Network (TxVSN).
NonCampusBasedInstruction
Descriptor


Short Description


 






01


College Campus Based Course


College course (usually a dual credit course) taught either on a college campus or a high school campus by an instructor not employed by the LEA. College courses taught on a high school campus by an LEA teacher with college credentials cannot be reported with NonCampusBasedInstruction 01 (College Campus Based Course).




02


Electronic/Internet/Correspondence Based/Video Conferencing Course


Any course that is taught not using an actual teacher (Classroom Position 01 (Teacher of Record), 02 (Assistant Teacher), 03 (Support Teacher), or 04 (Substitute Teacher)) in the classroom where the student(s) meet for the class. Examples include, but are not limited to, internet delivered curriculum, academic instructional software programs, video instruction (live or recorded), online courses, etc.




03


Non-District Teacher Providing Classroom Instruction Services


A course taught by a teacher that is employed by another LEA. The “classroom” could be at any suitable location. Do not use this for reporting college instructors.




04


Texas Virtual School Network (TxVSN) Online Schools program


This is a full-time virtual program available only to eligible students in grade levels 3 - 12 who are enrolled in an eligible LEA participating in the program. For additional information and rules refer to the Student Attendance Accounting Handbook. In order for a school to receive state funding for students enrolled in the TxVSN online school, all TxVSN Online Schools program course sections offered to students must be reported using this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor. (Valid through the 2026-2027 School Year)




05


Texas Virtual School Network (TxVSN) Statewide Online Course Catalog


This program provides a supplemental statewide online course catalog of high school, advanced placement, and dual credit courses to eligible students in grade levels 9 - 12 who are enrolled in the LEA. For additional information refer to the Student Attendance Accounting Handbook. In order for a school to receive state funding for students enrolled in courses offered through the TxVSN statewide course catalog, all TxVSN Statewide course catalog course sections offered to students must be reported using this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor. (Valid through the 2026-2027 School Year)




06


Non-Campus Teacher Providing Instruction at Another District Facility


These courses are taught in the district at a location that does not have its own campus number. An example of this would be when the CTE program courses are all taught at a central CTE location that is not eligible for its own campus number. These teachers are not associated with any other campus in the LEA.




07


Juvenile Justice Alternative Education Program (JJAEP) - TEC §37.011


These courses are always taught at a JJAEP that has been established in accordance with TEC 37.011 and are taught by teachers that are hired or are paid for by the JJAEP.




08


Credit by Exam


This NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor reflects those courses for which a student earned credit through the official credit by exam process.




09


Out of District DAEP Program


This NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor reflects those courses that a student is assigned to while placed in a DAEP that is physically located in another LEA. While this is similar to 03 (Non-District Teacher Providing Classroom Instruction Services), it is limited to those instances of a student attending a DAEP that is physically under the control of another school district or charter school.




10


Non-District PE Substitution Program


The use of this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor is limited to those cases where the LEA has authorized a student to earn PE credit by participating in a physical education activity that is not offered by the LEA. These include such things as gymnastic organizations, etc.




11


Optional Flexible School Day Online Dropout Recovery Program – TEC §29.081 (e-2)


The use of this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor is when a dropout recovery program is offered through an internet based online program. Among other provisions, online dropout recovery education programs are specifically required to:

include as part of its curriculum credentials, certifications, and other course offerings that relates directly to employment in the state;
provide an academic coach or local advocate for each student;
use an individual learning plan to monitor each student's progress, and
track the number of minutes the student is receiving instruction online.





12


Local Virtual Course


Any course where instruction and content are delivered synchronously or asynchronously primarily over the Internet. (TEC §30B.001(7))




13


Statewide Virtual Course


Virtual courses offered by school systems in the state to any student regardless of where the student is enrolled.




99


Other


The use of this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor is limited to those situations where no other NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor listed above applies.
 
For example, the teacher, if applicable, in the classroom is not employed by or under direct contract to the LEA. 
 
The use of this NonCampusBasedInstruction descriptor should be rare.
## DR5
ClassType (E1055) identifies the type of class providing instruction to students in particular class settings.
ClassType is used to differentiate classes providing instruction in a regular setting classroom from non-regular classrooms. Class size is computed on regular classes.
ClassType
Descriptor


Short Description


 






01


Regular


All settings not mentioned below including regular classroom, laboratory, or shop settings




02


Non-regular


All other settings (including but not limited to):

In-School Suspension
School-Community Guidance Center
Disciplinary Alternative Education School Program
Televised Instruction
Non-disciplinary Alternative Education
Special Education
Residential Care and Treatment Facility
CTEHours (E3011) indicate the number of contact hours assigned to a particular section of a course.
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day in the current school year the data elements in the SectionSet are associated to the section.
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day in the current school year the data elements in the SectionSet were associated to the section.

HighQualityPKProgram (E1580) Indicates campus/course/section participation in the High-Quality Prekindergarten Program consistent with requirements in TEC §29.167-29.171.
High-quality prekindergarten components are mandatory for classrooms serving eligible four-year-olds. This indicator should not be marked for classrooms serving only PK3 students.
PKStudentInstruction (E1558) indicates the prekindergarten student type of instruction.
PKSchoolType (E1555) indicates the type of prekindergarten program that is offered.

Descriptor


Short Description
