elements.business_rules_text:
=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
PEIMS Fall Enrollment Submission (6):
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is promoted for all students receiving special education services enrolled on the PEIMS Fall Enrollment snapshot date (first Friday in October).
PEIMS Fall Submission (1):
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is promoted for all students receiving special education services enrolled on the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October).
If the student exited from the special education program before the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October), then the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity must not be reported.
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
An LEA must report the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity for any student in membership (ADAEligibility 1-8) that was in a special education program at any time during the school year. If a student is receiving special education services, is enrolled not in membership (ADAEligibility 0 or 9) and the student receiving special education services has a restraint or discipline event, then the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity shall be reported. Additionally, if a student receiving special education services is enrolled, not in membership (ADAEligibility 0 or 9), and resides at a residential facility, then the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity shall be reported.
The Disability and MultiplyDisabled fields are used by TEA for the purposes of federal reporting of discipline and restraint data. The Disability and MultiplyDisabled are extracted for all students receiving special education services; the TEA Special Education department only joins this data with student discipline, restraint, and emergent bilingual data to determine which students should be included for federal reporting purposes.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported for all students receiving special education services based on the last day of school or the last day of the student’s enrollment whichever comes first.
## GR2
Residential Facility (RF) Tracker Submission:
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported by an LEA that serves students with disabilities residing in residential facilities within the LEA’s geographic boundaries or jurisdictions as soon as the student begins receiving services. All changes in the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity are promoted by TEA.
Suspended for the 2025-2026 School Year - Special Education Language Acquisition (SELA) Submission:
Data will not be collected for the SELA submission in the 2025-2026 school year.
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported by an LEA to report data on the language acquisition of children eight years of age or younger who are deaf or hard of hearing, identified with an auditory impairment or deaf/blindness using the Disability descriptors: 03 (Deaf or Hard of Hearing) or 05 (Deafblind). This entity is used to gather information about language acquisition services being provided to deaf or hard of hearing students.
Early Childhood Data System – Prekindergarten Submission:
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported by an LEA for prekindergarten students receiving special education services.
A new instance of the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity must be reported each time any of the data elements are modified in the LEA’s student information system (SIS). With each new instance, an updated BeginDate or EndDate indicates when the related data was changed.
Special Education Data System (SPEDS) – Summer Submission:
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported by an LEA for students exiting the ECSE program who have participated in the Child Outcomes Summary Process or with Secondary Transition goals determined in their IEP.
SPPI – 7 qualifying students will report both a StudentEarlychildhoodOutcomesEntrySet and a StudentEarlyChildhoodOutcomesExitSet.
SPPI – 13 qualifying students will report a StudentSecondaryTransitionSet.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
LocalEducationAgency
The LocalEducationAgency Reference represents the identifier assigned to a Local Education Agency (LEA).
Student Reference
The Student Reference represents the identifier assigned to the student.
Program Reference
The Program Reference represents the identifier assigned to the program.
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day a student is identified as being eligible to receive special education services.
The BeginDate must be the first instructional day a student has been classified with a Disability (C053) and one or more InstructionalSetting (C035). The BeginDate can be a date outside of the current school year, if the student began receiving special education services for the first time in a prior school year. The BeginDate should not change if a student moves from one school to a new school within the same LEA. The BeginDate should not be before a student has been classified with a Disability (C053) and one or more InstructionalSetting (C035).
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a student was eligible to receive special education services.
Note: An LEA may choose to enter an EndDate at the close of each school year for a student continuing to receive special education services. In this case, the new BeginDate should be the first day of the next school year instructional calendar, if the student was receiving special education services at the close of the prior school year and continues to receive special education services.
Examples:
LEA closes out every year:
For the 2024-2025 school year, the first instructional day for the Learning Elementary in Learning ISD is 08/19/2024. June Bug was enrolled on 08/19/2024 but was not classified with a Disability (C053) or an InstructionalSetting (C035). On 01/06/2025 June Bug was identified with InstructionalSetting (C035) 40 (Mainstream) and a Disability (C053) 08 (Specific Learning Disability). The BeginDate reported for June Bug would be 01/06/2025. The school year ends on 06/05/2025. The LEA adds an EndDate of 06/06/2025.
For the 2025-2026 school year, the first instructional day for the Learning Elementary in Learning ISD is 08/18/2025. June Bug was enrolled on 08/18/2025 and continued being identified with InstructionalSetting (C035) 40 (Mainstream) and a Disability (C053) 08 (Specific Learning Disability). The BeginDate reported for June Bug would be 08/18/2025.
On 09/17/2025, June Bug moves from Learning Elementary to River Elementary still in Learning ISD. The BeginDate for June Bug would be 08/18/2025 since River Elementary is still in Learning ISD.
LEA does not close out every year:
For the 2024-2025 school year, the first instructional day for the Tree Elementary in Woods ISD is 08/19/2024. Betty Butterfly was enrolled on 08/19/2024 but was not classified with a Disability (C053) or an InstructionalSetting (C035). On 01/06/2025 Betty Butterfly was identified with InstructionalSetting (C035) 40 (Mainstream) and a Disability (C053) 08 (Specific Learning Disability). The BeginDate reported for Betty Butterfly would be 01/06/2025. The school year ends on 06/05/2025.
For the 2025-2026 school year, the first instructional day for the Tree Elementary in Woods ISD is 08/18/2025. Betty Butterfly was enrolled on 08/18/2025 and continued being identified with InstructionalSetting (C035) 40 (Mainstream) and a Disability (C053) 08 (Specific Learning Disability). The BeginDate reported for Betty Butterfly would be 01/06/2025.
On 09/17/2025, Betty Butterfly moves from Tree Elementary to Sunflower Elementary still in Woods ISD. The BeginDate for June Bug would be 01/06/2025 since Sunflower Elementary is still in Woods ISD.
PreferredHomeCommunicationMethod (E1661) identifies the preferred unique communication method used by the child at home.
PreferredHomeCommunicationMethod is reported for the Special Education Language Acquisition (SELA) Submission only.
## DR2
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>StudentSPEDProgramAssociationSet
The StudentSPEDProgramAssociationSet captures the special education programs and related services a student receives and the ProgramBeginDate and ProgramEndDate associated with the following data elements.
MedicallyFragile (E0999) indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services is:
- in the age range of birth to 22 years, and
- has a serious, ongoing illness or a chronic condition that has lasted or is anticipated to last at least 12 or more months or has required at least one month of hospitalization, and that requires daily, ongoing medical treatments and monitoring by appropriately trained personnel which may include parents or other family members, and
- requires the routine use of medical device or of assistive technology to compensate for the loss of usefulness of a body function needed to participate in activities of daily living, and
- lives with ongoing threat to his or her continued well-being.
MultiplyDisabled (E0882) indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services has been designated as multiply disabled by the admission, review, and dismissal committee. [See 19 TAC §89.1040(c)(6).]
A student who is multiply disabled has a combination of disabilities and meets all of the conditions listed in 19 TAC §89.1040(c)(6). Not all students who have more than one disability are determined to be multiply disabled.
A student should not be reported as multiply disabled unless an ARD committee has determined that the student has a combination of disabilities included in TAC §89.1040 and meets all of the conditions listed below:
- The student's disability is expected to continue indefinitely; and
- The student's disabilities severely impair performance in two or more of the following areas:

psychomotor skills
self-care skills
communication
social and emotional development
cognition
- psychomotor skills
- self-care skills
- communication
- social and emotional development
- cognition
Multiply disabled is not a disability in the Disability descriptor table. Rather, all the disabilities that lead to a determination of multiply disabled are reported through the OrderOfDisability (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary). The determination of multiply disabled is indicated in MultiplyDisabled data element.
LEAOfRDSPDService (E1527) indicates the LEA identification number of the Regional Day School Program for the Deaf (RDSPD) Fiscal Agent that is providing RDSPD services.
This LEA must be registered with the Texas Education Agency.
ChildCountFunding (E0832) indicates under which federal program the student receiving special education and related services is counted.
ChildCountFunding eligible students include students receiving special education services, ages three through 21, who:
- meet the requirements of 19 TAC §89.1040 and 19 TAC §89.1050;
- are enrolled and receiving special education and related services through an IEP as of the PEIMS Fall snapshot date;
- are receiving services through an Individualized Services Program;
- have on file a current individualized education program or individualized services plan; and
- have on file a current full and individual evaluation
Students receiving special education services who meet requirements should be reported. These students are at least three on the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October) and less than 22 years of age on September 1.
Pursuant to 34 CFR §300.102, students with disabilities who graduate under 19 TAC §89.1070(c) and return to school are included on the IDEA Part B child count.
ECSEServiceLocation (E1077) indicates whether or not the Early Childhood Special Education (ECSE) student received their early childhood special education services in a regular early childhood program, which is defined as a program that is designed for typically developing children ages three through five (not in kindergarten) and is not specifically or primarily designed for children with disabilities and includes (at the time of the placement decision) a majority of at least 50 percent of non-disabled children (i.e., children without an individualized education program (IEP)).
Additional information about Early Childhood Special Education (ECSE) Services can be found in the TEA Student Attendance Accounting Handbook.
ProgramBeginDate (E3047) indicates the month, day, and year the student special education program association set becomes true of the student.
ProgramEndDate (E3048) is the first day after the last instructional day any data element in the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociationSet common type changes or becomes false for the student.
## DR3
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>InstructionalSettingSet
The InstructionalSettingSet common type captures the instructional setting for a student and the InstructionalSettingBeginDate and InstructionalSettingEndDate associated with the InstructionalSetting data element.
InstructionalSetting (E0173) identifies the setting used in providing instruction to students.
Only one InstructionalSetting should be reported at any time for a student. A student who is receiving speech therapy services and is not receiving instructional services through any other instructional setting should have an InstructionalSetting of 00 (No Instructional Setting) reported. A student who receives speech therapy services and who also receives instructional services through another instructional setting should be reported with the descriptor for the primary setting (not 00) and a SpecialEducationProgramService 25 (Special Education Student Rec Speech Therapy and Other SPED Instr Setting).
InstructionalSettingBeginDate (E3025) is the first instructional day a student is assigned to the InstructionalSetting descriptor.
InstructionalSettingEndDate (E3026) is the first day after the last instructional day a student was assigned to the InstructionalSetting descriptor.
## DR4
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>Disability
The Disability common type captures the disability category identified for a student according to the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), as ordered by severity.
Disability (E3015) indicates the disability category that describes a child’s impairment.
Multiple instances of this data element can be reported.
A student identified with developmental delay is either:
- a student between the ages of 3 through 9 who is evaluated by a multidisciplinary team for at least one disability category under 19 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) 89.1040 and whose evaluation data indicates a need for special education and related services and show evidence of, but does not clearly confirm, the presence of the suspected disability or disabilities due to the child's young age. In these cases, the ARD committee may determine that data supports identification of developmental delay in one or more of the following areas: physical development, cognitive development, communication development, social or emotional development, or adaptive development. To use this eligibility category, multiple sources of data must converge to indicate the student has a developmental delay by meeting one of the criteria listed at 19 TAC 89.1040(c)(13)(A)-(C);
- both a reevaluation and ARD committee meeting must be completed prior to the student turning 10 years old.
- a student less than 3 who is reported with a SPEDProgramSvc 20 (Early Childhood Intervention Services) and is identified with a developmental delay based on their early childhood intervention (ECI) services.
Disability 12 (Developmental Delay) can only be reported for students receiving special education services who are less than 10 years of age on the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October)
## DR5
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>Disability>DisabilitySet
The DisabilitySet captures additional information related to the Disability and the DisabilitySetBeginDate and DisabilitySetEndDate data elements.
OrderOfDisability (E3039) is the order by severity of student’s disabilities: (1) Primary, (2) Secondary, and (3) Tertiary.
EligibilityDateDisabilities (E1723) indicates the date upon which a student who is deaf or hard of hearing is eligible for services.
The EligibilityDateDisabilities data element is only used by the SELA collection.
DisabilitySetBeginDate (E3016) indicates the month, day, and year the order of the disability becomes true.
DisabilitySetEndDate (E3017) indicates the month, day, and year the order of the disability becomes false.
## DR6
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>SPEDProgramSvcSet
The SPEDProgramSvcSet common type captures the type of special education program services that a student participates in or receives services from and the ServiceBeginDate and ServiceEndDate associated with the SPEDProgramSvc data element.
SPEDProgramSvc (E3058) defines the services provided by an education organization to populations of students associated with a special education program.
01 – Social Work Services




Definition




The Social Work Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, social work services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34.)




Special Instructions




Social workers must be licensed by the Texas State Board of Examiners and must hold a bachelor’s or master’s degree.




Former Data Element Name and Number




SOCIAL-WORK-SERVICES-IND-CODE (E0849)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
02-09 – Interpreting Services




Definition




The Interpreting Services special education program service indicates whether the student who is deaf and receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, interpreting services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34(c)(4).)




Special Instructions




Interpreting services include the following, when used with respect to children who are deaf or hard of hearing: Oral transliteration services, cued language transliteration services, sign language transliteration and interpreting services, and transcription services, such as communication access real-time translation (CART), C-Print, and TypeWell; and special interpreting services for children who are deaf-blind.
 
Note: The language above is from 34 CFR §300.34(c)(4). Interpreting services for students who are deaf shall be provided by an interpreter who is certified by the Registry of Interpreters for the Deaf or the Texas Commission for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing.
Note: New federal requirements do not allow emergency permits – TEA is no longer issuing them.
 
In the event that an ARD committee recommends more than one type of interpreting services, i.e., sign language transliteration services and communication access real-time translation (CART) services, the ARD committee is responsible for providing attendance personnel the appropriate interpreting services type. In no case, should attendance personnel be responsible for determining the appropriate interpreting services type for a student.




Former Data Element Name and Number




INTERPRETING-SERVICES-TYPE-CODE (E1040)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
10 – Psychological Services




Definition




The Psychological Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, psychological services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34.)




Special Instructions




Psychological services must be provided by a professional who is licensed by the Texas State Board of Examiners of Psychologists as a Licensed Specialist in School Psychology (LSSP), psychologist or a psychological associate. (See TEC §21.003 and 19 TAC §89.1131.)




Former Data Element Name and Number




PSYCHOLOGICAL-SERVICES-IND-CODE (E0846)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
11 – Physical Therapy Services




Definition




The Physical Therapy Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, physical therapy services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34.)




Special Instructions




Physical therapy must be provided by a professional licensed by the Executive Council of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy Examiners. A physical therapy assistant (LPTA) may provide physical therapy services under the supervision of a licensed physical therapist in accordance with the standards of the profession. (See TEC §21.003 and 19 TAC §89.1131.)




Former Data Element Name and Number




PHYSICAL-THERAPY-IND-CODE (E0845)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
12 – Recreation Including Therapeutic Recreation




Definition




The Recreation Including Therapeutic Recreation special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, recreation services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34.)




Special Instructions




Recreation includes assessment of leisure function, therapeutic recreation services, recreation programs in schools and community agencies, and leisure education.




Former Data Element Name and Number




RECREATION-IND-CODE (E0847)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
13 – Counseling Services




Definition




The Counseling Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services receive, or is scheduled to receive, counseling services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34.)




Special Instructions




Counseling services must be provided in the are of specialization by a qualified professional credentialed to practice in Texas. (19 TAC §89.1131(a))




Former Data Element Name and Number




COUNSELING-SERVICES-IND-CODE (E0840)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
14 – Orientation and Mobility




Definition




The Orientation and Mobility special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, orientation and mobility training services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34.)




Special Instructions




Orientation and mobility training includes those aids, methods, services, and skills which enable visually impaired individuals to move from one place to another with confidence, safety, and purpose. Orientation and mobility instruction must be provided by a professional who meets the requirements explained in TEC §21.003 and 19 TAC §89.1131.




Former Data Element Name and Number




ORIENT-MOBILITY-TRNG-IND-CODE (E0844)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
15 – Medical Services




Definition




The Medical Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, medical diagnostic services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34).




Special Instructions




Medical diagnostic services must be provided by a licensed physician. (See TEC §21.003 and 19 TAC §89.1131.)




Former Data Element Name and Number




MEDICAL-DIAGNOSTIC-SERV-IND-CODE (E0841)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
16 – School Health And/Or School Nurse Services




Definition




The School Health And/Or School Nurse Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, school health services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34.)




Special Instructions




School health services and school nurse services are those provided to students receiving special education and related services in addition to those routinely available to all students and are designed to enable a child with a disability to receive FAPE as described in the child’s IEP. School nurse services are those provided by a qualified school nurse. School health services may be provided by a qualified school nurse or other qualified person.




Former Data Element Name and Number




SCHOOL-HEALTH-SERVICES-IND-CODE (E0848)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
17 – Assistive Technology Device or Related Services




Definition




The Assistive Technology Device or Related Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, an assistive technology device or service during the current school semester.
 
Assistive technology device means any item, piece of equipment, or product system, whether acquired commercially off the shelf, modified, or customized, that is used to increase, maintain, or improve the functional capabilities of children with disabilities. The term does not include a medical device that is surgically implanted or the replacement of such device.
 
Assistive technology service means any service that directly assists a child with a disability in the selection, acquisition, or use of an assistive technology device.
 
The term Assistive technology service includes:

the evaluation of the needs of a child with a disability, including a functional evaluation of the child in the child's customary environment;
purchasing, leasing, or otherwise providing for the acquisition of assistive technology devices by children with disabilities;
selecting, designing, fitting, customizing, adapting, applying, maintaining, repairing, or replacing assistive technology devices;
coordinating and using other therapies, interventions, or services with assistive technology devices, such as those associated with existing education and rehabilitation plans and programs;
training or technical assistance for a child with a disability or, if appropriate, that child's family; and
training or technical assistance for professionals (including individuals providing education or rehabilitation services), employers, or other individuals who provide services to, employ, or are otherwise substantially involved in the major life functions of children with disabilities.

 
Assistive technology devices and services must be made available if required as part of a child’s special education, as a related service, or as supplementary aids and services. (See 34 CFR §§300.5-300.6 and 19 TAC §89.1050.)




Special Instructions




The full and individual evaluation, including a written report, shall be completed in accordance with 34 CFR §300.121, 300.301, 300.303-300.311; TEC §29.004; and 19 TAC §89.1040. Each school district shall establish at least one admission, review, and dismissal committee that shall make decisions concerning eligibility determinations, development of the individualized education program, consideration of assistive technology, development of the behavior improvement plans, and placement of a student referred for special education and related services in accordance with 34 CFR §300.5, §300.6, §300.34, §300.41, §300.42, §300.105(a), and 34 CFR §§300.320-300.324; state statute; and SBOE rules. (See 19 TAC §89.1050.)




Former Data Element Name and Number




ASSISTIVE-TECH-INDICATOR-CODE (E0997)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
## DR7
18 – Audiological Services




Definition




The Audiological Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, audiological services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34.)




Special Instructions




Audiological services must be provided by a professional who holds a valid state license as an audiologist. (See TEC §21.002, §21.003, §29.304, and 19 TAC §89.1131.)




Former Data Element Name and Number




AUDIOLOGICAL-SERV-IND-CODE (E0838)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
19 – Early Childhood Special Education Services




Definition




The Early Childhood Special Education Services special education program service indicates whether the preschool student, age three through five years old and not in kindergarten, is receiving any special education and related services from the school district or charter school in any setting(s) or environment. [See 19 TAC §89.1035, and 34 CFR §300.101(b)]




Special Instructions




Students, three through five years old (not in kindergarten), previously reported with the Early Childhood Special Education Services descriptor, who are six years old as of the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October), should not be reported with the descriptor.
 
The Early Childhood Special Education (ECSE) Services can only be reported for students receiving special education services who are at least three and less than six years of age and not in kindergarten on the PEIMS Fall snapshot date.  All students receiving special education services under IDEA Part B who are ages three through five (not in kindergarten), as of the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October), are participating in ECSE program and must be reported as Early Childhood Special Education Services regardless of their disability or instructional setting.
 
ECSE is a Texas term which refers to a federally funded program under IDEA Part B which is targeted specifically for three- through five-year-old (not in kindergarten) students receiving special education and related services.  ECSE includes students whose only special education service is speech therapy regardless of where the services are provided.
 
Each LEA shall ensure that a continuum of alternative placements is available to meet the needs of students with disabilities for special education and related services. (34CFR §300.115) For three- through five-year-old (not in kindergarten) students receiving ECSE services, the LEA continuum could include but is not limited to:

LEA or Community Childcare Programs
Prekindergarten Programs
Head Start Programs
Home Environment
Special Education Resource Settings
Special Education Self Contained Settings
LEA or Community Therapy Settings (Speech, OT/PT, etc.)





Former Data Element Name and Number




PRESCHL-PROG-CHLDRN-WITH-DISAB-IND-CD (E0899)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
20 – Early Childhood Intervention Services




Definition




The Early Childhood Intervention Services special education program service indicates whether the infant or toddler, from birth through age two, is participating in the early childhood intervention program. (See Texas Human Resources Code §73.001 and §73.021)




Special Instructions




The early childhood intervention (ECI) program is operated through the Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC). If the district does not operate an ECI program, this descriptor is not used to identify infants and toddlers with visual impairments or who are deaf or hard of hearing who receive hearing and vision services from the district under the Memorandum of Understanding between the HHSC and the Texas Education Agency.
 
Refer to Section IV of the Student Attendance Accounting Handbook for information on coding these children. [See 19 TAC §89.63(d).]
 
Early Childhood Intervention Program should be used only for students’ from birth through age two, as of the PEIMS Fall snapshot date. When the student turns three, the child may receive early childhood special education (ECSE) services if determined to be eligible.




Former Data Element Name and Number




EARLY-CHILDHOOD-INTERV-IND-CODE (E0900)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
21 – Occupational Therapy 




Definition




The Occupational Therapy special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, occupational therapy services during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34.)




Special Instructions




Occupational therapy must be provided by a professional who is licensed by the Executive Council of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy Examiners. A licensed occupational therapy assistant may provide occupational therapy services under the supervision of a licensed occupational therapist in accordance with the standards of the profession. (See TEC §21.003 and 19 TAC §89.1131.)




Former Data Element Name and Number




OCCUPATIONAL-THERAPY-IND-CODE (E0843)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
22 – Receiving Instructional Services from RDSPD




Definition




The Receiving Instructional Services from RDSPD special education program service indicates the student is receiving instructional services from the regional day school program for the deaf.




Special Instructions




All students in the RDSPD must have a disabling condition of 03 (Deaf and Hard of Hearing) or 05 (Deaf-Blindness) as either their primary, secondary, or tertiary disability. A student can be reported with both disabilities in the appropriate order of disabling condition. The information must reflect exactly what the IEP states.
 
All students who are in the RDSPD may generate average daily attendance (ADA) based on their ADAEligibility and their InstructionalSetting. These general education funds in regular education and in special education can be used to supplement the costs of the RDSPD.
 
The TEA RDSPD Shared Services Arrangement (SSA) Procedures document requires all SSAs to include two or more LEAs.
 
The fiscal agent for the RDSPD is often the LEA where students attend classes. There are some Education Service Centers (ESC) that serve as RDSPD fiscal agents.




Former Data Element Name and Number




REG-DAY-SCH-PROG-DEAF-CODE (E0833)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
PEIMS Fall Submission (1):
Only one LEA may report data on a student participating in the Regional Day School Program for the Deaf (RDSPD). Sending and receiving LEAs must reach an agreement in writing regarding which LEA will report data for the student. It is recommended that the RDSPD fiscal agent report data for students served, except for itinerant students.
23 – 25 – Speech Therapy 




Definition




The Speech Therapy special education program service indicates whether the student is receiving speech pathology/speech therapy services through the special education program in a speech therapy instructional arrangement. [See 19 TAC §89.63 (c)(4).]




Special Instructions




Students who are provided speech therapy services only are not eligible to be counted for any other instructional arrangement.
 
Speech therapy/speech pathology services must be provided by a professional with a TEA certificate in Speech & Hearing Therapy, Speech Therapy, School Speech-Language Pathology or with a license from the State Board of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology. A Speech-Language Pathology assistant may provide speech language pathology services under the supervision of a speech-language pathologist.




Former Data Element Name and Number




SPEECH-THERAPY-INDICATOR-CODE (E0794)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
26 – Special Education Transportation Services




Definition




The Special Education Transportation Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, special transportation services (due to his or her disability) during the current school semester. (See 34 CFR §300.34 and TEC §42.155.)




Special Instructions




The eligibility for transportation services for students receiving special education and related services is described in TEC §42.155.




Former Data Element Name and Number




TRANSPORTATION-INDICATOR-CODE (E0851)




Submission




PEIMS Fall, RF-Tracker
ServiceBeginDate (E3055) is the first instructional day a student is assigned to the SPEDProgramSvc descriptor.
ServiceEndDate (E3056) is the first day after the last instructional day a student was assigned to the SPEDProgramSvc descriptor.
## DR8
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>TierOfIntensitySetThe TierOfIntensitySet common type captures the tier of intensity for a student and the TierOfIntensityBeginDate and TierOfIntensityEndDate associated with the TierOfIntensity data element.
TierOfIntensity (E3153) refers to the level of support and intervention provided to special education students based on their individual learning needs.
TierOfIntensityBeginDate (E3157) is the first instructional day a student is assigned to the TierOfIntensity descriptor.
TierOfIntensityEndDate  (E3158) is the first day after the last instructional day a student was assigned to the TierOfIntensity descriptor.
## DR9
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>SPEDServiceGroupSetThe SPEDServiceGroupSet common type captures the SPED service group for a student and the SPEDServiceGroupBeginDate and SPEDServiceGroupEndDate associated with the SPEDServiceGroup data element.
SPEDServiceGroup (E3159) indicates the category or group of students based on the type, intensity, or setting of special education services the student receives.
SPEDServiceGroupBeginDate (E3160) is the first instructional day a student is assigned to the SPEDServiceGroup descriptor.
SPEDServiceGroupEndDate (E3161) is the first day after the last instructional day a student was assigned to the SPEDServiceGroup descriptor.
## DR10
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>NumberOfMinutesInSPEDSetThe NumberOfMinutesInSPEDSet common type captures the average number of minutes per day a student receives special education services in a special education classroom or setting and the NumberOfMinutesInSPEDBeginDate and NumberOfMinutesInSPEDEndDate.
NumberOfMinutesInSPED (E3162) indicates the average number of minutes per day that a student receives special education services in a special education classroom or setting, as determined by the Admission, Review, and Dismissal (ARD) Committee.
NumberOfMinutesInSPEDBeginDate (E3163) is the first instructional day a student receives the reported number of minutes in special education.
NumberOfMinutesInSPEDEndDate (E3164)  is the first day after the last instructional day a student received the reported number of minutes in special education.
## DR11
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>EducationalEnvironmentSetThe EducationalEnvironmentSet common type captures the educational environment setting in which a student receives special education and related services and the EducationalEnvironmentBeginDate and EducationalEnvironmentEndDate.
EducationalEnvironment (E3155) indicates the setting in which a student receives special education and related services.
EducationalEnvironmentBeginDate (E3175) is the first instructional day a student is assigned to the EducationalEnvironment descriptor.
EducationalEnvironmentEndDate (E3176) is the first day after the last instructional day a student was assigned to the EducationalEnvironment descriptor.
## DR12
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>LanguageAcquisition
The LanguageAcquisition common type captures the language acquisition services a student has received. Multiple instances of the LanguageAcquisition common type can be reported if a student receives more than one type of service. The LanguageAcquisition common type is only used by the SELA collection.
LangAcqServicesProvided (E1662) indicates the specific language acquisition services provided to the student.
One or more services may be provided. If the LEA does not provide language acquisition services, 00 (Services not Provided) should be reported.
Corresponding data elements FrequencyOfServices and HoursSpentReceivingServices must also be provided when the LangAcqServicesProvided is reported as any value other than 00 (Services not Provided).
FrequencyOfServices (E1663) identifies the frequency with which a student receives services.
Choose the lowest increment of time that is applicable for this service. For example, if service is provided for more than five (5) hours a day, 02 (Weekly) is a better choice than 03 (Monthly).
Multiple instances of this data element can be reported. FrequencyOfServices must be provided for each 01 (Direct) or 02 (Indirect/Consultative) LangAcqServicesProvided reported.
If the LEA does not provide language acquisition services, FrequencyOfServices should not be reported.
HoursSpentReceivingServices(E1664) identifies the amount of time in which the student receives services.
Multiple instances of this data element can be reported. HoursSpentReceivingServices must be provided for each 01 (Direct) or 02 (Indirect/Consultative) LangAcqServicesProvided reported.
If the LEA does not provide language acquisition services, HoursSpentReceivingServices should not be reported.
## DR13
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>HearingAmplification
The HearingAmplification common type captures the hearing amplification device(s), access and use for a student. Multiple instances of the HearingAmplification common type can be reported if a student uses more than one device. The HearingAmplification common type is only used by the SELA collection.
HearingAmplificationType (E1665) identifies the type of hearing amplification device used by the student.
One or more devices may be identified. Multiple instances of this data element can be reported. For each HearingAmplificationType reported that is not 00 (Not Applicable), a corresponding response for HearingAmplificationAccess must also be reported.
HearingAmplificationAccess (E1666) identifies whether the student has access to the hearing amplification devise for the full-day or partial day for each HearingAmplificationType reported.
Multiple instances of this data element can be reported. HearingAmplificationAccess must be provided for each HearingAmplificationType reported unless HearingAmplificationType reported is 00 (Not Applicable).
HearingAmplificationDailyUse (E1667) identifies the average amount of time the hearing amplification device is used in a day based on the HearingAmplificationAccess reported.
Multiple instances of this data element can be reported. HearingAmplificationDailyUse is only reported if HearingAmplificationAccess is 02 (Partial Day).
## DR14
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>Assessment
The Assessment common type captures the assessments conducted to evaluate a student’s language acquisition. Multiple instances of the Assessment common type can be reported if more than one tool or assessment is used. The Assessment common type is only used by the SELA collection.
ToolOrAssessmentUsed (E1668) identifies the tool or assessment used to assess the student’s language acquisition.
More than one tool or assessment may be reported. For each ToolOrAssessmentUsed reported that is not 00 (Not Assessed), a corresponding response for data element E1669 AssessmentResultsObtained must also be reported.
AssessmentResultsObtained (E1669) identifies the results of the tool or assessment used to assess the student’s language acquisition.
Multiple instances of this data element can be reported. AssessmentResultsObtained must be provided for each ToolOrAssessmentUsed reported unless ToolOrAssessmentUsed reported is 00 (Not Assessed).
## DR15
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>StudentResidentialFacilityAssociation
The StudentResidentialFacilityAssociation common type captures whether a student is enrolled in a residential facility and the DateEnteredRF and DateExitedRF associated with the student’s enrollment in a residential facility. The StudentResidentialFacilityAssociation common type is only used by the RF-Tracker collection.
ResidentialFacilityId (E1627) indicates the unique residential facility identification number registered with the Texas Education Agency.
DateEnteredRF (E1630) is the first instructional day in the current school year a student is assigned to the residential facility.
DateExitedRF (E1631) is the first day after the last instructional day a student is assigned to the residential facility.
If the student is still residing in the residential facility at the end of the school year, do not report DateExitedRF.
## DR16
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>StudentResidentialFacilityAssociation>StudentResFacAssocSet
The StudentResFacAssocSet common type captures a point in time set of indicators for a student’s interaction with a residential facility and the StudentResFacAssocSetBeginDate and StudentResFacAssocSetEndDate associated with the StudentResFacAssocSet data elements. The StudentResFacAssocSet common type is only used by the RF-Tracker collection. When any data element in the set is modified, the LEA should end the set and report a new set with a new StudentResFacAssocSetBeginDate.
StudentResFacAssocSetBeginDate (E3064) indicates the first month, day, and year any data element in the StudentResFacAssocSet common type becomes true for the student.
StudentResFacAssocSetEndDate (E3065) is the first day afer the last instructional day any data element in the StudentResFacAssocSet common type changes or becomes false for the student.
AttendanceZoneCampus (E1633) is the nine-digit identifying number (assigned by the TEA) of the campus the student is expected to attend based on the geographic location (address) of the residential facility in which the student resides.
EducatedAtResidentialFacility (E1634) indicates whether a student is educated at or in the general location of a residential facility.
SurrogateParentAssigned (E1635) indicates whether the student has been assigned a surrogate parent.
NumberOtherStudentsAssignedSameSurrogateParent (E1636) indicates how many other students have been assigned to the same surrogate parent.
ResidentialFacilityStudentSchoolDayLength (E1637) indicates the number of minutes the residential facility student receives instruction based on the Individualized Education Program (IEP).
CampusIdOfEnrollmentSchoolDayLength (E1638) indicates the number of instructional minutes in a school day for a non-disabled peer at the campus of enrollment.
## DR17
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>StudentEarlyChildhoodOutcomesEntrySet
The StudentEarlyChildhoodOutcomesEntrySet captures the rating information for SPPI-7 when a student enters the Early Childhood Special Education (ECSE) program.
ECSESocialEmotionalEntrySkillsRating (E3100) indicates the student’s level of functioning in positive social-emotional skills (including social relationships) upon entry into the early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
ECSEKnowledgeEntrySkillsRating (E3101) indicates the student's level of functioning in the acquisition and use of knowledge and skills (including early language/communication) upon entry into the early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
ECSEAppropriateFunctioningEntrySkillsRating (E3102) indicates the student's level of functioning in the use of appropriate behaviors to meet their needs upon entry into the early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
## DR18
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>StudentEarlyChildhoodOutcomesExitSet
The StudentEarlyChildhoodOutcomesExitSet captures the rating information for SPPI-7 when a student exits the Early Childhood Special Education (ECSE) program.
ECSEServiceExitReason (E3103) indicates the reason a student exited from a local education agency’s (LEA’s) early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
All students with an entry record who meet the exit criteria must have an exit record including a reason for exit.
If ECSEServiceExitReason is Transitions to kindergarten (01) or Dismissed by Admission Review and Dismissal (ARD) Committee (02), the LEA must also report the following:
- ECSESocialEmotionalExitSkillsRating (E3104),
- ECSEExitSocialEmotionalNewSkills (E3105)
- ECSEKnowledgeExitSkillsRating (E3106)
- ECSEExitKnowledgeNewSkills (E3107)
- ECSEAppropriateFunctioningExitSkillsRating (E3108)
- ECSEExitAppropriateFunctioningNewSkills (E3109)
ECSESocialEmotionalExitSkillsRating (E3104) indicates the student's level of functioning in positive social-emotional skills (including social relationships) upon exit from the early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
ECSEExitSocialEmotionalNewSkills (E3105) indicates if the child has shown any new skills or behaviors related to positive social-emotional skills (including positive social relationships) since the local education agency’s initial skills rating (child outcomes summary).
ECSEKnowledgeExitSkillsRating (E3106) indicates the student's level of functioning in the acquisition and use of knowledge and skills (including early language/communication) upon exit from the early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
ECSEExitKnowledgeNewSkills (E3107) indicates if the child has shown any new skills or behaviors related to acquiring and using knowledge and skills since the local education agency’s initial skills rating (child outcomes summary).
ECSEAppropriateFunctioningExitSkillsRating (E3108) indicates the student's level of functioning in the use of appropriate behaviors to meet their needs upon exit from the early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
ECSEExitAppropriateFunctioningNewSkills (E3109) indicates if the child has shown any new skills or behaviors related to taking appropriate action to meet needs since the local education agency’s initial skills rating (child outcomes summary).
## DR19
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>StudentSecondaryTransitionSet
The StudentSecondaryTransitionSet captures the information for SPPI-13.
SecondaryTransitionARDMeetingDate (E3110) is the most recent date the admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee met to update a student’s individualized education program (IEP) to include:
- appropriate measurable postsecondary goals that are annually updated and based upon an age-appropriate transition assessment.
- transition services, including courses of study, that will reasonably enable the student to meet those postsecondary goals, and
- annual IEP goals related to the student’s transition service needs.
Note: There also must be evidence that the student was invited to the IEP Team meeting where transition services are to be discussed and evidence that, if appropriate, a representative of any participating agency that is likely to be responsible for providing or paying for transition services, including, if appropriate, pre-employment tranistion services, was invited to the IEP Team meeting with the prior consent of the parent or student who has reached the age of majority.
SecondaryTransitionIEPReviewDate (E3099) is the date the Local Education Agency (LEA) reviewed the student’s individualized education program (IEP) folder for documentation of the SPPI-13 indicator requirement.
MeasurableSecondaryGoals (E3111) indicates whether or not there were appropriate measurable postsecondary goals in the areas of training, education, employment, and, where appropriate, independent living skills in a student’s individualized education program (IEP).
UpdatedSecondaryGoals (E3112) indicates whether or not the postsecondary goals set in the individualized education program (IEP) were updated annually.
TransitionAssessment (E3113) indicates whether or not there is evidence that the measurable postsecondary goals were based on age-appropriate transition assessments.
IEPTransitionServices (E3114) indicates whether or not the student’s individualized education program (IEP) includes transition services that will reasonably enable the student to meet their postsecondary goals.
CourseStudySecondaryGoals (E3115) indicates whether or not the transition services included courses of study that will reasonably enable the student to meet their postsecondary goals.
TransitionServiceNeeds (E3116) indicates whether or not there is/are annual individualized education program (IEP) goals related to the student’s transition service needs.
ARDInvitedStudent (E3117) indicates whether or not there is documented evidence the student was invited to the Admission, Review, and Dismissal (ARD) Committee meeting where transition services were discussed.
ARDInvitedRepresentative (E3118) indicates whether or not there is evidence that a representative of any participating agency was invited to the Admission, Review, and Dismissal (ARD) Committee meeting with the prior consent of the parent or student who has reached age of majority

elements.business_rules_text:
=== Entity-level rules (shared) ===
General Requirements: ## GR1
PEIMS Fall Enrollment Submission (6):
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is promoted for all students receiving special education services enrolled on the PEIMS Fall Enrollment snapshot date (first Friday in October).
PEIMS Fall Submission (1):
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is promoted for all students receiving special education services enrolled on the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October).
If the student exited from the special education program before the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October), then the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity must not be reported.
PEIMS Summer Submission (3):
An LEA must report the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity for any student in membership (ADAEligibility 1-8) that was in a special education program at any time during the school year. If a student is receiving special education services, is enrolled not in membership (ADAEligibility 0 or 9) and the student receiving special education services has a restraint or discipline event, then the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity shall be reported. Additionally, if a student receiving special education services is enrolled, not in membership (ADAEligibility 0 or 9), and resides at a residential facility, then the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity shall be reported.
The Disability and MultiplyDisabled fields are used by TEA for the purposes of federal reporting of discipline and restraint data. The Disability and MultiplyDisabled are extracted for all students receiving special education services; the TEA Special Education department only joins this data with student discipline, restraint, and emergent bilingual data to determine which students should be included for federal reporting purposes.
PEIMS Extended Year Submission (4):
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported for all students receiving special education services based on the last day of school or the last day of the student’s enrollment whichever comes first.
## GR2
Residential Facility (RF) Tracker Submission:
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported by an LEA that serves students with disabilities residing in residential facilities within the LEA’s geographic boundaries or jurisdictions as soon as the student begins receiving services. All changes in the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity are promoted by TEA.
Suspended for the 2025-2026 School Year - Special Education Language Acquisition (SELA) Submission:
Data will not be collected for the SELA submission in the 2025-2026 school year.
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported by an LEA to report data on the language acquisition of children eight years of age or younger who are deaf or hard of hearing, identified with an auditory impairment or deaf/blindness using the Disability descriptors: 03 (Deaf or Hard of Hearing) or 05 (Deafblind). This entity is used to gather information about language acquisition services being provided to deaf or hard of hearing students.
Early Childhood Data System – Prekindergarten Submission:
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported by an LEA for prekindergarten students receiving special education services.
A new instance of the StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity must be reported each time any of the data elements are modified in the LEA’s student information system (SIS). With each new instance, an updated BeginDate or EndDate indicates when the related data was changed.
Special Education Data System (SPEDS) – Summer Submission:
The StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation Entity is reported by an LEA for students exiting the ECSE program who have participated in the Child Outcomes Summary Process or with Secondary Transition goals determined in their IEP.
SPPI – 7 qualifying students will report both a StudentEarlychildhoodOutcomesEntrySet and a StudentEarlyChildhoodOutcomesExitSet.
SPPI – 13 qualifying students will report a StudentSecondaryTransitionSet.

Data Element Reporting Requirements: ## DR1
LocalEducationAgency
The LocalEducationAgency Reference represents the identifier assigned to a Local Education Agency (LEA).
Student Reference
The Student Reference represents the identifier assigned to the student.
Program Reference
The Program Reference represents the identifier assigned to the program.
BeginDate (E3010) is the first instructional day a student is identified as being eligible to receive special education services.
The BeginDate must be the first instructional day a student has been classified with a Disability (C053) and one or more InstructionalSetting (C035). The BeginDate can be a date outside of the current school year, if the student began receiving special education services for the first time in a prior school year. The BeginDate should not change if a student moves from one school to a new school within the same LEA. The BeginDate should not be before a student has been classified with a Disability (C053) and one or more InstructionalSetting (C035).
EndDate (E3020) is the first day after the last instructional day a student was eligible to receive special education services.
Note: An LEA may choose to enter an EndDate at the close of each school year for a student continuing to receive special education services. In this case, the new BeginDate should be the first day of the next school year instructional calendar, if the student was receiving special education services at the close of the prior school year and continues to receive special education services.
Examples:
LEA closes out every year:
For the 2024-2025 school year, the first instructional day for the Learning Elementary in Learning ISD is 08/19/2024. June Bug was enrolled on 08/19/2024 but was not classified with a Disability (C053) or an InstructionalSetting (C035). On 01/06/2025 June Bug was identified with InstructionalSetting (C035) 40 (Mainstream) and a Disability (C053) 08 (Specific Learning Disability). The BeginDate reported for June Bug would be 01/06/2025. The school year ends on 06/05/2025. The LEA adds an EndDate of 06/06/2025.
For the 2025-2026 school year, the first instructional day for the Learning Elementary in Learning ISD is 08/18/2025. June Bug was enrolled on 08/18/2025 and continued being identified with InstructionalSetting (C035) 40 (Mainstream) and a Disability (C053) 08 (Specific Learning Disability). The BeginDate reported for June Bug would be 08/18/2025.
On 09/17/2025, June Bug moves from Learning Elementary to River Elementary still in Learning ISD. The BeginDate for June Bug would be 08/18/2025 since River Elementary is still in Learning ISD.
LEA does not close out every year:
For the 2024-2025 school year, the first instructional day for the Tree Elementary in Woods ISD is 08/19/2024. Betty Butterfly was enrolled on 08/19/2024 but was not classified with a Disability (C053) or an InstructionalSetting (C035). On 01/06/2025 Betty Butterfly was identified with InstructionalSetting (C035) 40 (Mainstream) and a Disability (C053) 08 (Specific Learning Disability). The BeginDate reported for Betty Butterfly would be 01/06/2025. The school year ends on 06/05/2025.
For the 2025-2026 school year, the first instructional day for the Tree Elementary in Woods ISD is 08/18/2025. Betty Butterfly was enrolled on 08/18/2025 and continued being identified with InstructionalSetting (C035) 40 (Mainstream) and a Disability (C053) 08 (Specific Learning Disability). The BeginDate reported for Betty Butterfly would be 01/06/2025.
On 09/17/2025, Betty Butterfly moves from Tree Elementary to Sunflower Elementary still in Woods ISD. The BeginDate for June Bug would be 01/06/2025 since Sunflower Elementary is still in Woods ISD.
PreferredHomeCommunicationMethod (E1661) identifies the preferred unique communication method used by the child at home.
PreferredHomeCommunicationMethod is reported for the Special Education Language Acquisition (SELA) Submission only.
## DR2
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>StudentSPEDProgramAssociationSet
The StudentSPEDProgramAssociationSet captures the special education programs and related services a student receives and the ProgramBeginDate and ProgramEndDate associated with the following data elements.
MedicallyFragile (E0999) indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services is:
- in the age range of birth to 22 years, and
- has a serious, ongoing illness or a chronic condition that has lasted or is anticipated to last at least 12 or more months or has required at least one month of hospitalization, and that requires daily, ongoing medical treatments and monitoring by appropriately trained personnel which may include parents or other family members, and
- requires the routine use of medical device or of assistive technology to compensate for the loss of usefulness of a body function needed to participate in activities of daily living, and
- lives with ongoing threat to his or her continued well-being.
MultiplyDisabled (E0882) indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services has been designated as multiply disabled by the admission, review, and dismissal committee. [See 19 TAC §89.1040(c)(6).]
A student who is multiply disabled has a combination of disabilities and meets all of the conditions listed in 19 TAC §89.1040(c)(6). Not all students who have more than one disability are determined to be multiply disabled.
A student should not be reported as multiply disabled unless an ARD committee has determined that the student has a combination of disabilities included in TAC §89.1040 and meets all of the conditions listed below:
- The student's disability is expected to continue indefinitely; and
- The student's disabilities severely impair performance in two or more of the following areas:

psychomotor skills
self-care skills
communication
social and emotional development
cognition
- psychomotor skills
- self-care skills
- communication
- social and emotional development
- cognition
Multiply disabled is not a disability in the Disability descriptor table. Rather, all the disabilities that lead to a determination of multiply disabled are reported through the OrderOfDisability (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary). The determination of multiply disabled is indicated in MultiplyDisabled data element.

17 – Assistive Technology Device or Related Services




Definition




The Assistive Technology Device or Related Services special education program service indicates whether the student receiving special education and related services received, or is scheduled to receive, an assistive technology device or service during the current school semester.
 
Assistive technology device means any item, piece of equipment, or product system, whether acquired commercially off the shelf, modified, or customized, that is used to increase, maintain, or improve the functional capabilities of children with disabilities. The term does not include a medical device that is surgically implanted or the replacement of such device.
 
Assistive technology service means any service that directly assists a child with a disability in the selection, acquisition, or use of an assistive technology device.
 
The term Assistive technology service includes:

the evaluation of the needs of a child with a disability, including a functional evaluation of the child in the child's customary environment;
purchasing, leasing, or otherwise providing for the acquisition of assistive technology devices by children with disabilities;
selecting, designing, fitting, customizing, adapting, applying, maintaining, repairing, or replacing assistive technology devices;
coordinating and using other therapies, interventions, or services with assistive technology devices, such as those associated with existing education and rehabilitation plans and programs;
training or technical assistance for a child with a disability or, if appropriate, that child's family; and
training or technical assistance for professionals (including individuals providing education or rehabilitation services), employers, or other individuals who provide services to, employ, or are otherwise substantially involved in the major life functions of children with disabilities.

 
Assistive technology devices and services must be made available if required as part of a child’s special education, as a related service, or as supplementary aids and services. (See 34 CFR §§300.5-300.6 and 19 TAC §89.1050.)




Special Instructions




The full and individual evaluation, including a written report, shall be completed in accordance with 34 CFR §300.121, 300.301, 300.303-300.311; TEC §29.004; and 19 TAC §89.1040. Each school district shall establish at least one admission, review, and dismissal committee that shall make decisions concerning eligibility determinations, development of the individualized education program, consideration of assistive technology, development of the behavior improvement plans, and placement of a student referred for special education and related services in accordance with 34 CFR §300.5, §300.6, §300.34, §300.41, §300.42, §300.105(a), and 34 CFR §§300.320-300.324; state statute; and SBOE rules. (See 19 TAC §89.1050.)

19 – Early Childhood Special Education Services




Definition




The Early Childhood Special Education Services special education program service indicates whether the preschool student, age three through five years old and not in kindergarten, is receiving any special education and related services from the school district or charter school in any setting(s) or environment. [See 19 TAC §89.1035, and 34 CFR §300.101(b)]




Special Instructions




Students, three through five years old (not in kindergarten), previously reported with the Early Childhood Special Education Services descriptor, who are six years old as of the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October), should not be reported with the descriptor.
 
The Early Childhood Special Education (ECSE) Services can only be reported for students receiving special education services who are at least three and less than six years of age and not in kindergarten on the PEIMS Fall snapshot date.  All students receiving special education services under IDEA Part B who are ages three through five (not in kindergarten), as of the PEIMS Fall snapshot date (last Friday in October), are participating in ECSE program and must be reported as Early Childhood Special Education Services regardless of their disability or instructional setting.
 
ECSE is a Texas term which refers to a federally funded program under IDEA Part B which is targeted specifically for three- through five-year-old (not in kindergarten) students receiving special education and related services.  ECSE includes students whose only special education service is speech therapy regardless of where the services are provided.
 
Each LEA shall ensure that a continuum of alternative placements is available to meet the needs of students with disabilities for special education and related services. (34CFR §300.115) For three- through five-year-old (not in kindergarten) students receiving ECSE services, the LEA continuum could include but is not limited to:

LEA or Community Childcare Programs
Prekindergarten Programs
Head Start Programs
Home Environment
Special Education Resource Settings
Special Education Self Contained Settings
LEA or Community Therapy Settings (Speech, OT/PT, etc.)

The StudentEarlyChildhoodOutcomesExitSet captures the rating information for SPPI-7 when a student exits the Early Childhood Special Education (ECSE) program.
ECSEServiceExitReason (E3103) indicates the reason a student exited from a local education agency’s (LEA’s) early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
All students with an entry record who meet the exit criteria must have an exit record including a reason for exit.
If ECSEServiceExitReason is Transitions to kindergarten (01) or Dismissed by Admission Review and Dismissal (ARD) Committee (02), the LEA must also report the following:
- ECSESocialEmotionalExitSkillsRating (E3104),
- ECSEExitSocialEmotionalNewSkills (E3105)
- ECSEKnowledgeExitSkillsRating (E3106)
- ECSEExitKnowledgeNewSkills (E3107)
- ECSEAppropriateFunctioningExitSkillsRating (E3108)
- ECSEExitAppropriateFunctioningNewSkills (E3109)
ECSESocialEmotionalExitSkillsRating (E3104) indicates the student's level of functioning in positive social-emotional skills (including social relationships) upon exit from the early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
ECSEExitSocialEmotionalNewSkills (E3105) indicates if the child has shown any new skills or behaviors related to positive social-emotional skills (including positive social relationships) since the local education agency’s initial skills rating (child outcomes summary).
ECSEKnowledgeExitSkillsRating (E3106) indicates the student's level of functioning in the acquisition and use of knowledge and skills (including early language/communication) upon exit from the early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
ECSEExitKnowledgeNewSkills (E3107) indicates if the child has shown any new skills or behaviors related to acquiring and using knowledge and skills since the local education agency’s initial skills rating (child outcomes summary).
ECSEAppropriateFunctioningExitSkillsRating (E3108) indicates the student's level of functioning in the use of appropriate behaviors to meet their needs upon exit from the early childhood special education (ECSE) program.
ECSEExitAppropriateFunctioningNewSkills (E3109) indicates if the child has shown any new skills or behaviors related to taking appropriate action to meet needs since the local education agency’s initial skills rating (child outcomes summary).
## DR19
StudentSpecialEducationProgramAssociation>StudentSecondaryTransitionSet
The StudentSecondaryTransitionSet captures the information for SPPI-13.
SecondaryTransitionARDMeetingDate (E3110) is the most recent date the admission, review, and dismissal (ARD) committee met to update a student’s individualized education program (IEP) to include:
- appropriate measurable postsecondary goals that are annually updated and based upon an age-appropriate transition assessment.
- transition services, including courses of study, that will reasonably enable the student to meet those postsecondary goals, and
- annual IEP goals related to the student’s transition service needs.
Note: There also must be evidence that the student was invited to the IEP Team meeting where transition services are to be discussed and evidence that, if appropriate, a representative of any participating agency that is likely to be responsible for providing or paying for transition services, including, if appropriate, pre-employment tranistion services, was invited to the IEP Team meeting with the prior consent of the parent or student who has reached the age of majority.
SecondaryTransitionIEPReviewDate (E3099) is the date the Local Education Agency (LEA) reviewed the student’s individualized education program (IEP) folder for documentation of the SPPI-13 indicator requirement.
MeasurableSecondaryGoals (E3111) indicates whether or not there were appropriate measurable postsecondary goals in the areas of training, education, employment, and, where appropriate, independent living skills in a student’s individualized education program (IEP).
UpdatedSecondaryGoals (E3112) indicates whether or not the postsecondary goals set in the individualized education program (IEP) were updated annually.
TransitionAssessment (E3113) indicates whether or not there is evidence that the measurable postsecondary goals were based on age-appropriate transition assessments.
IEPTransitionServices (E3114) indicates whether or not the student’s individualized education program (IEP) includes transition services that will reasonably enable the student to meet their postsecondary goals.
CourseStudySecondaryGoals (E3115) indicates whether or not the transition services included courses of study that will reasonably enable the student to meet their postsecondary goals.
TransitionServiceNeeds (E3116) indicates whether or not there is/are annual individualized education program (IEP) goals related to the student’s transition service needs.
ARDInvitedStudent (E3117) indicates whether or not there is documented evidence the student was invited to the Admission, Review, and Dismissal (ARD) Committee meeting where transition services were discussed.
ARDInvitedRepresentative (E3118) indicates whether or not there is evidence that a representative of any participating agency was invited to the Admission, Review, and Dismissal (ARD) Committee meeting with the prior consent of the parent or student who has reached age of majority
